@code {
    private readonly List<string> _errors = [];

    private Person? _person;
    private bool _hasPassword;

    [CascadingParameter]
    private HttpContext HttpContext { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm(FormName = "change-password")]
    private ChangePasswordInputModel ChangeInput { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm(FormName = "add-password")]
    private AddPasswordInputModel AddInput { get; set; } = default!;

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
    {
        // BL0008: the form POSTs bind these themselves and may assign null, so the defaults live here.
        ChangeInput ??= new();
        AddInput ??= new();

        Person? user = await UserManager.GetUserAsync(HttpContext.User);
        if (user is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo(AccountRoutes.SignIn);
            return;
        }

        _person = user;
        _hasPassword = user.PasswordHash is not null;
    }

    private async Task ChangeAsync()
    {
        Person? user = _person;
        if (user is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo(AccountRoutes.SignIn);
            return;
        }

        IdentityResult result = await UserManager.ChangePasswordAsync(
            user,
            ChangeInput.CurrentPassword,
            ChangeInput.NewPassword);

        if (!result.Succeeded)
        {
            _errors.Clear();
            _errors.AddRange(result.Errors.Select(error => error.Description));
            return;
        }

        await CompleteAsync(user, "password-changed");
    }

    private async Task AddAsync()
    {
        Person? user = _person;
        if (user is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo(AccountRoutes.SignIn);
            return;
        }

        // AddPasswordAsync re-reads the stored hash and refuses if one is already set, so a stale form
        // posted after a password was added elsewhere fails cleanly rather than overwriting it.
        IdentityResult result = await UserManager.AddPasswordAsync(user, AddInput.NewPassword);

        if (!result.Succeeded)
        {
            _errors.Clear();
            _errors.AddRange(result.Errors.Select(error => error.Description));
            return;
        }

        await CompleteAsync(user, "password-added");
    }

    private async Task CompleteAsync(Person user, string outcome)
    {
        // The subject is also the actor: this is the person changing their own password, so
        // actorPersonIdentifier stays null (the §8.2 convention — a non-null actor means somebody
        // else did it, as an administrative reset does).
        await SecurityEventLog.RecordAsync(
            user.PersonIdentifier,
            actorPersonIdentifier: null,
            SecurityEventType.PasswordChanged);

        // UpdatePasswordHash rotated the security stamp; re-issue the cookie so this session survives
        // the change instead of being cut at the next revalidation (§3.1).
        await SignInManager.RefreshSignInAsync(user);

        Navigation.NavigateTo($"{AccountRoutes.Profile}?done={outcome}");
    }

    private sealed class ChangePasswordInputModel
    {
        [Required(ErrorMessage = "Enter your current password.")]
        public string CurrentPassword { get; set; } = string.Empty;

        [Required(ErrorMessage = "Choose a new password.")]
        [MinLength(12, ErrorMessage = "Passwords are at least 12 characters (§3.2) — a short sentence works.")]
        public string NewPassword { get; set; } = string.Empty;

        [Required(ErrorMessage = "Repeat the new password.")]
        [Compare(nameof(NewPassword), ErrorMessage = "The two entries do not match.")]
        public string ConfirmPassword { get; set; } = string.Empty;
    }

    private sealed class AddPasswordInputModel
    {
        [Required(ErrorMessage = "Choose a password.")]
        [MinLength(12, ErrorMessage = "Passwords are at least 12 characters (§3.2) — a short sentence works.")]
        public string NewPassword { get; set; } = string.Empty;

        [Required(ErrorMessage = "Repeat the password.")]
        [Compare(nameof(NewPassword), ErrorMessage = "The two entries do not match.")]
        public string ConfirmPassword { get; set; } = string.Empty;
    }
}

@code {
    private readonly List<string> _errors = [];

    [CascadingParameter]
    private HttpContext HttpContext { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm]
    private ChangePasswordInputModel Input { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery]
    private string? ReturnUrl { get; set; }

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
    {
        // BL0008: a form POST binds Input itself and may assign null, so the default lives here
        // rather than in a property initializer the binder would silently discard.
        Input ??= new();

        Person? user = await UserManager.GetUserAsync(HttpContext.User);
        if (user is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo(AccountRoutes.SignIn);
            return;
        }

        // Nothing outstanding (stale link, or the flag cleared in another tab): move along. The
        // database is consulted rather than the claim so a just-cleared flag never re-traps anyone.
        if (!user.MustChangePassword && HttpContext.Request.Method == HttpMethods.Get)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo(ObligationsEnforcement.SafeLocalReturnUrl(ReturnUrl));
        }
    }

    private async Task ChangePasswordAsync()
    {
        Person? user = await UserManager.GetUserAsync(HttpContext.User);
        if (user is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo(AccountRoutes.SignIn);
            return;
        }

        string destination = ObligationsEnforcement.SafeLocalReturnUrl(ReturnUrl);

        if (!user.MustChangePassword)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo(destination);
            return;
        }

        // Clear the flag on the entity BEFORE the change: ChangePasswordAsync persists the entity
        // (UpdateAsync) only on its success path, so the new hash and the cleared flag commit in one
        // store update — and a failed attempt persists nothing.
        user.MustChangePassword = false;
        IdentityResult result = await UserManager.ChangePasswordAsync(
            user,
            Input.CurrentPassword,
            Input.NewPassword);

        if (!result.Succeeded)
        {
            user.MustChangePassword = true;
            _errors.Clear();
            _errors.AddRange(result.Errors.Select(error => error.Description));
            return;
        }

        await SecurityEventLog.RecordAsync(
            user.PersonIdentifier,
            actorPersonIdentifier: null,
            SecurityEventType.ForcedPasswordChangeCompleted);

        // Re-issue the cookie: fresh security stamp, and the obligation claim disappears with it, so
        // the middleware releases this principal on the very next request.
        await SignInManager.RefreshSignInAsync(user);

        Navigation.NavigateTo(destination);
    }

    private sealed class ChangePasswordInputModel
    {
        [Required(ErrorMessage = "Enter the temporary password you signed in with.")]
        public string CurrentPassword { get; set; } = string.Empty;

        [Required(ErrorMessage = "Choose a new password.")]
        [MinLength(12, ErrorMessage = "Passwords are at least 12 characters (§3.2) — a short sentence works.")]
        public string NewPassword { get; set; } = string.Empty;

        [Required(ErrorMessage = "Repeat the new password.")]
        [Compare(nameof(NewPassword), ErrorMessage = "The two entries do not match.")]
        public string ConfirmPassword { get; set; } = string.Empty;
    }
}

@page "/account/enroll-totp"
@attribute [ExcludeFromInteractiveRouting]
@attribute [Authorize]
@using MyRestaurant.Domain.Authentication
@inject UserManager<Person> UserManager
@inject SignInManager<Person> SignInManager

@* The voluntary authenticator page (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §3.4, §4.2): any signed-in user can
   enroll here, and an already-enrolled user can regenerate their recovery codes. Static SSR, like
   every account page, because confirming enrollment rotates the security stamp and re-issues the
   cookie — a Blazor circuit cannot write cookies. This page is NOT in the obligations-exempt list:
   it is a normal authenticated destination, so a user with an outstanding obligation is routed to
   the relevant pipeline page by the middleware, never here. The forced re-enrollment obligation has
   its own page (EnrollTotpRequired.razor).

   Two POSTs share this page, each with its own form name and bound model:
     • "enroll-totp-confirm" — confirm a scanned secret (carries the protected ticket + the code);
     • "enroll-totp-regenerate" — regenerate recovery codes for an already-enrolled account.
   The GET decides which UI to show from the derived enrollment state (secret present or not). *@

<section class="panel account-panel">
    <p class="eyebrow">Security</p>

    @if (_recoveryCodes is not null)
    {
        <h1>Save your recovery codes</h1>

@code {
    private bool _enrolled;
    private int _remainingRecoveryCodes;
    private TotpEnrollmentStart? _start;
    private IReadOnlyList<string>? _recoveryCodes;
    private string? _recoveryCodesLede;
    private string? _errorMessage;

    [CascadingParameter]
    private HttpContext HttpContext { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm(FormName = "enroll-totp-confirm")]
    private ConfirmInputModel ConfirmInput { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm(FormName = "enroll-totp-regenerate")]
    private RegenerateInputModel RegenerateInput { get; set; } = default!;

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
    {
        // BL0008: a form POST binds these itself and may assign null, so defaults live here.
        ConfirmInput ??= new();
        RegenerateInput ??= new();

        Person? user = await UserManager.GetUserAsync(HttpContext.User);
        if (user is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo(AccountRoutes.SignIn);
            return;
        }

        // A GET (or a POST that did not already produce codes to show) renders the state-appropriate
        // UI; if the account is not enrolled, a fresh secret + QR + ticket is prepared to display.
        _enrolled = await UserManager.GetTwoFactorEnabledAsync(user);
        if (_enrolled)
        {
            _remainingRecoveryCodes = await Enrollment.CountRecoveryCodesAsync(user, HttpContext.RequestAborted);
        }
        else
        {
            _start = Enrollment.BeginEnrollment(user);
        }
    }

    private async Task ConfirmAsync()
    {
        Person? user = await UserManager.GetUserAsync(HttpContext.User);
        if (user is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo(AccountRoutes.SignIn);
            return;
        }

        // Already enrolled (e.g. a stale tab): nothing to confirm.
        if (await UserManager.GetTwoFactorEnabledAsync(user))
        {
            _enrolled = true;
            _start = null;
            _remainingRecoveryCodes = await Enrollment.CountRecoveryCodesAsync(user, HttpContext.RequestAborted);
            return;
        }

        (TotpEnrollmentConfirmation confirmation, TotpEnrollmentResult? result) = await Enrollment.ConfirmAsync(
            user,
            ConfirmInput.ProtectedTicket,
            ConfirmInput.Code,
            forced: false,
            HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        switch (confirmation)
        {
            case TotpEnrollmentConfirmation.Succeeded:
                // Confirm rotated the security stamp; refresh the cookie so this session survives the
                // next stamp revalidation. The cookie is written during this SSR submit handler,
                // before the recovery codes are rendered below, so showing them here is safe.
                await SignInManager.RefreshSignInAsync(user);
                _recoveryCodes = result!.RecoveryCodes;
                _recoveryCodesLede = "Your authenticator is now enrolled.";
                _enrolled = true;
                _start = null;
                break;

            case TotpEnrollmentConfirmation.InvalidCode:
                // Keep the same secret/QR/ticket so the user can retry the code they just mistyped;
                // if the ticket has since expired, ResumeEnrollment returns null and we start fresh.
                _errorMessage = "That code did not verify. Codes rotate every 30 seconds — check the app and try the current one.";
                _start = Enrollment.ResumeEnrollment(user, ConfirmInput.ProtectedTicket) ?? Enrollment.BeginEnrollment(user);
                break;

            case TotpEnrollmentConfirmation.TicketInvalid:
            default:
                // The scanned secret expired or the ticket was unusable: issue a fresh QR to scan.
                _errorMessage = "This setup step expired. Scan the new QR code and enter a fresh six-digit code.";
                _start = Enrollment.BeginEnrollment(user);
                break;
        }
    }

    private async Task RegenerateAsync()
    {
        Person? user = await UserManager.GetUserAsync(HttpContext.User);
        if (user is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo(AccountRoutes.SignIn);
            return;
        }

        // Regeneration only makes sense once enrolled; a non-enrolled POST falls back to setup.
        if (!await UserManager.GetTwoFactorEnabledAsync(user))
        {
            _enrolled = false;
            _start = Enrollment.BeginEnrollment(user);
            return;
        }

        TotpEnrollmentResult result = await Enrollment.RegenerateRecoveryCodesAsync(user, HttpContext.RequestAborted);
        _recoveryCodes = result.RecoveryCodes;
        _recoveryCodesLede = "Your recovery codes have been regenerated.";
        _enrolled = true;
    }

    private sealed class ConfirmInputModel
    {
        public string ProtectedTicket { get; set; } = string.Empty;

        [Required(ErrorMessage = "Enter the six-digit code from your authenticator app.")]
        public string Code { get; set; } = string.Empty;
    }

    private sealed class RegenerateInputModel
    {
    }
}

@page "/account/enroll-totp-required"
@attribute [ExcludeFromInteractiveRouting]
@attribute [Authorize]
@using MyRestaurant.Domain.Authentication
@inject UserManager<Person> UserManager
@inject SignInManager<Person> SignInManager
@inject TotpEnrollment Enrollment
@inject NavigationManager Navigation

@* Obligation (2) of the post-authentication pipeline (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §3.5): forced TOTP
   re-enrollment after an administrative reset wiped an enrolled secret and set `must_enroll_totp`.
   ObligationsMiddleware routes every request here (this route is exempt) until the flag clears.

   Same mechanics as the voluntary page, three differences that suit an obligation:
     • the copy explains WHY re-enrollment is required, not "would you like to";
     • ConfirmAsync is called with forced: true, so it records `forced_totp_enrollment_completed`
       and clears `must_enroll_totp` in the same store update that writes the secret (mirroring the
       forced password page's one-update pattern);
     • there is no recovery-code regeneration branch — the point here is to (re)enroll.
   On GET: if the obligation is already clear (stale link / cleared in another tab) the visitor is
   passed along; if a password change is ALSO outstanding, the earlier pipeline step wins and we
   send them there (both pipeline pages are exempt, so navigating between them by hand is allowed).
   Static SSR: confirmation rotates the stamp and re-issues the cookie, which a circuit cannot do. *@

<PageTitle>Re-enroll your authenticator</PageTitle>

<section class="panel account-panel">
    <p class="eyebrow">Action required</p>

    @if (_recoveryCodes is not null)
    {
        <h1>Save your new recovery codes</h1>
        <p class="lede">
            Your authenticator is enrolled again. Each code works once — store them somewhere safe. If
            you lose your authenticator, a recovery code is the only way back in.
        </p>

        <ul class="recovery-codes" aria-label="Recovery codes">
            @foreach (string recoveryCode in _recoveryCodes)
            {

@code {
    private TotpEnrollmentStart? _start;
    private IReadOnlyList<string>? _recoveryCodes;
    private string? _errorMessage;
    private string _destination = "/";

    [CascadingParameter]
    private HttpContext HttpContext { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm(FormName = "enroll-totp-required")]
    private ConfirmInputModel Input { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery]
    private string? ReturnUrl { get; set; }

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
    {
        // BL0008: a form POST binds Input itself and may assign null, so the default lives here.
        Input ??= new();

        _destination = ObligationsEnforcement.SafeLocalReturnUrl(ReturnUrl);

        Person? user = await UserManager.GetUserAsync(HttpContext.User);
        if (user is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo(AccountRoutes.SignIn);
            return;
        }

        // The database is consulted rather than the claim so a just-cleared flag never re-traps anyone.
        if (HttpContext.Request.Method == HttpMethods.Get)
        {
            // Password change is the earlier pipeline step; if it is also outstanding, defer to it.
            if (user.MustChangePassword)
            {
                Navigation.NavigateTo(AccountRoutes.ForcedPasswordChange);
                return;
            }

            if (!user.MustEnrollTotp)
            {
                Navigation.NavigateTo(_destination);
                return;
            }
        }

        // Still outstanding: prepare a secret + QR + ticket to display.
        _start = Enrollment.BeginEnrollment(user);
    }

    private async Task ConfirmAsync()
    {
        Person? user = await UserManager.GetUserAsync(HttpContext.User);
        if (user is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo(AccountRoutes.SignIn);
            return;
        }

        // Cleared elsewhere in the meantime: move along instead of showing a stale demand.
        if (!user.MustEnrollTotp)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo(_destination);
            return;
        }

        (TotpEnrollmentConfirmation confirmation, TotpEnrollmentResult? result) = await Enrollment.ConfirmAsync(
            user,
            Input.ProtectedTicket,
            Input.Code,
            forced: true,
            HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        switch (confirmation)
        {
            case TotpEnrollmentConfirmation.Succeeded:
                // Confirm cleared must_enroll_totp and rotated the stamp; refresh the cookie so the
                // stale obligation claim does not keep the middleware redirecting here (and so the
                // session survives the next stamp revalidation). Cookie is written in this SSR submit
                // handler, before the recovery codes render below.
                await SignInManager.RefreshSignInAsync(user);
                _recoveryCodes = result!.RecoveryCodes;
                _start = null;
                break;

            case TotpEnrollmentConfirmation.InvalidCode:
                _errorMessage = "That code did not verify. Codes rotate every 30 seconds — check the app and try the current one.";
                _start = Enrollment.ResumeEnrollment(user, Input.ProtectedTicket) ?? Enrollment.BeginEnrollment(user);
                break;

            case TotpEnrollmentConfirmation.TicketInvalid:
            default:
                _errorMessage = "This setup step expired. Scan the new QR code and enter a fresh six-digit code.";
                _start = Enrollment.BeginEnrollment(user);
                break;
        }
    }

    private sealed class ConfirmInputModel
    {
        public string ProtectedTicket { get; set; } = string.Empty;

        [Required(ErrorMessage = "Enter the six-digit code from your authenticator app.")]
        public string Code { get; set; } = string.Empty;
    }
}

@code {
    private IList<UserPasskeyInfo>? _passkeys;
    private string? _statusMessage;
    private string? _errorMessage;

    [CascadingParameter]
    private HttpContext HttpContext { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm(FormName = "add-passkey")]
    private PasskeyInputModel Input { get; set; } = default!;

    // Shared by every per-row "passkey-{id}" form; only the submitted row's values arrive.
    [SupplyParameterFromForm]
    private string? Action { get; set; }

    [SupplyParameterFromForm]
    private string? CredentialId { get; set; }

    [SupplyParameterFromForm]
    private string? NewName { get; set; }

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery(Name = "status")]
    private string? Status { get; set; }

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
    {
        // BL0008: a form POST binds Input itself and may assign null, so the default lives here.
        Input ??= new();
        _statusMessage = Status;

        Person? user = await UserManager.GetUserAsync(HttpContext.User);
        if (user is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo(AccountRoutes.SignIn);
            return;
        }

        _passkeys = await UserManager.GetPasskeysAsync(user);
    }

    private async Task AddPasskeyAsync()
    {
        Person? user = await UserManager.GetUserAsync(HttpContext.User);
        if (user is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo(AccountRoutes.SignIn);
            return;
        }

        if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(Input.Error))
        {
            await FailAsync(user, "That passkey could not be added. Please try again.");
            return;
        }

        if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(Input.CredentialJson))
        {
            await FailAsync(user, "Your browser did not provide a passkey.");
            return;
        }

        PasskeyAttestationResult attestation = await SignInManager.PerformPasskeyAttestationAsync(Input.CredentialJson);
        if (!attestation.Succeeded || attestation.Passkey is null)
        {
            await FailAsync(user, "That passkey could not be registered. Please try again.");
            return;
        }

        // The authenticator does not supply a name; give it a readable default the user can change.
        UserPasskeyInfo passkey = attestation.Passkey;
        passkey.Name = $"Passkey added {RestaurantClock.Date(DateTimeOffset.UtcNow)}";

        IdentityResult added = await UserManager.AddOrUpdatePasskeyAsync(user, passkey);
        if (!added.Succeeded)
        {
            await FailAsync(user, "The passkey could not be saved to your account.");
            return;
        }

        await SecurityEventLog.RecordAsync(
            user.PersonIdentifier, actorPersonIdentifier: null, SecurityEventType.PasskeyRegistered, HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        Redirect("Passkey added. You can rename it below.");
    }

    private async Task UpdatePasskeyAsync()
    {
        Person? user = await UserManager.GetUserAsync(HttpContext.User);
        if (user is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo(AccountRoutes.SignIn);
            return;
        }

        byte[] credentialId;
        try
        {
            credentialId = Base64Url.DecodeFromChars(CredentialId);
        }
        catch (FormatException)
        {
            await FailAsync(user, "That passkey could not be identified.");
            return;
        }

        if (string.Equals(Action, "delete", StringComparison.Ordinal))
        {
            IdentityResult removed = await UserManager.RemovePasskeyAsync(user, credentialId);
            if (!removed.Succeeded)
            {
                await FailAsync(user, "The passkey could not be removed.");
                return;
            }

            await SecurityEventLog.RecordAsync(
                user.PersonIdentifier, actorPersonIdentifier: null, SecurityEventType.PasskeyRemoved, HttpContext.RequestAborted);
            Redirect("Passkey removed.");
            return;
        }

        if (string.Equals(Action, "rename", StringComparison.Ordinal))
        {
            UserPasskeyInfo? existing = await UserManager.GetPasskeyAsync(user, credentialId);
            if (existing is null)
            {
                await FailAsync(user, "That passkey no longer exists.");
                return;
            }

            // Blank keeps the current name; the store's update path writes only the mutable fields,
            // so the public key and backup-eligible bit captured at registration are untouched.
            existing.Name = string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(NewName) ? existing.Name : NewName.Trim();
            IdentityResult renamed = await UserManager.AddOrUpdatePasskeyAsync(user, existing);
            if (!renamed.Succeeded)
            {
                await FailAsync(user, "The passkey could not be renamed.");
                return;
            }

            Redirect("Passkey renamed.");
            return;
        }

        await FailAsync(user, "That action was not recognized.");
    }

    // Re-load the list and show an error on the same render (no redirect, so no status query needed).
    private async Task FailAsync(Person user, string message)
    {
        _errorMessage = message;
        _passkeys = await UserManager.GetPasskeysAsync(user);
    }

    // Post/redirect/get: carry a one-line confirmation back through the query string.
    private void Redirect(string status)
        => Navigation.NavigateTo($"{AccountRoutes.Passkeys}?status={Uri.EscapeDataString(status)}");
}

@code {
    private readonly List<string> _errors = [];

    private Person? _person;
    private IList<string> _roles = [];
    private int _passkeyCount;
    private string? _flashMessage;

    [CascadingParameter]
    private HttpContext HttpContext { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm(FormName = "account-details")]
    private ProfileInputModel Input { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery]
    private string? Done { get; set; }

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
    {
        // BL0008: the form POST binds Input itself and may assign null, so the default lives here
        // rather than in a property initializer the binder would silently discard.
        Input ??= new();

        Person? user = await UserManager.GetUserAsync(HttpContext.User);
        if (user is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo(AccountRoutes.SignIn);
            return;
        }

        _person = user;
        _roles = await UserManager.GetRolesAsync(user);
        _passkeyCount = (await UserManager.GetPasskeysAsync(user)).Count;

        // Prefill only on GET: on a POST the binder has already filled Input from the submitted form,
        // and overwriting it here would throw away what the person just typed.
        if (HttpContext.Request.Method == HttpMethods.Get)
        {
            Input.DisplayName = user.DisplayName;
            Input.EmailAddress = user.EmailAddress;
            Input.PhoneNumber = user.PhoneNumber;
            _flashMessage = FlashFor(Done);
        }
    }

    private async Task SaveDetailsAsync()
    {
        Person? user = _person;
        if (user is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo(AccountRoutes.SignIn);
            return;
        }

        ProfileDetails details = ProfileDetails.Normalize(Input.DisplayName, Input.EmailAddress, Input.PhoneNumber);

        IReadOnlyList<string> problems = details.Validate();
        if (problems.Count > 0)
        {
            _errors.Clear();
            _errors.AddRange(problems);
            return;
        }

        if (details.SameAs(user.DisplayName, user.EmailAddress, user.PhoneNumber))
        {
            RedirectWithOutcome("details-unchanged");
            return;
        }

        // The display name is a claim (RestaurantClaimsPrincipalFactory), so note whether it moved
        // before the entity is mutated — that decides whether the cookie has to be re-issued.
        bool displayNameChanged = !string.Equals(user.DisplayName, details.DisplayName, StringComparison.Ordinal);

        user.DisplayName = details.DisplayName;
        user.EmailAddress = details.EmailAddress;
        user.PhoneNumber = details.PhoneNumber;

        // One store update writes all three columns (DapperUserStore.UpdateAsync persists the whole
        // row). UserManager.UpdateAsync validates and normalizes first; it does NOT rotate the
        // security stamp, which is right — none of these three fields is a credential, so live
        // sessions have no reason to be invalidated.
        IdentityResult result = await UserManager.UpdateAsync(user);
        if (!result.Succeeded)
        {
            _errors.Clear();
            _errors.AddRange(result.Errors.Select(error => error.Description));
            return;
        }

        if (displayNameChanged)
        {
            // Re-issue the cookie so the new name shows immediately rather than at the next
            // five-minute security-stamp revalidation (§3.1).
            await SignInManager.RefreshSignInAsync(user);
        }

        RedirectWithOutcome("details-saved");
    }

    private void RedirectWithOutcome(string outcome)
        => Navigation.NavigateTo($"{AccountRoutes.Profile}?done={outcome}");

    private static string? FlashFor(string? outcome) => outcome switch
    {
        "details-saved" => "Your details were saved.",
        "details-unchanged" => "Nothing changed.",
        "password-changed" => "Your password was changed.",
        "password-added" => "Your password was set. You can now sign in with it.",
        _ => null,
    };

    private sealed class ProfileInputModel
    {

@page "/sign-in"
@attribute [ExcludeFromInteractiveRouting]
@inject SignInManager<Person> SignInManager
@inject NavigationManager Navigation

@* The sign-in page (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §3.3, §3.5, §4.1). Static SSR on purpose: issuing the
   authentication cookie needs a real HTTP response, which a Blazor circuit does not have. The form
   is a plain full-page POST (EditForm in SSR emits the antiforgery token itself). Auditing and
   metering happen centrally in RestaurantSignInManager, never here.

   Password and passkey share one form. It uses OnSubmit (not OnValidSubmit) so the passkey button can
   skip the password DataAnnotations: the passkey-submit element writes the assertion credential into
   Input.Passkey and submits natively, and the handler runs PasskeySignInAsync on that before it
   validates anything. A passkey sign-in never gets a TOTP challenge (§3.5) — that is guaranteed in the
   sign-in manager, not here. The username carries autocomplete="username webauthn" so browsers can
   surface a discoverable passkey inline (conditional mediation). *@

<PageTitle>Sign in</PageTitle>

<section class="panel account-panel">
    <p class="eyebrow">MyRestaurant</p>
    <h1>Sign in</h1>

    @if (HttpContext.User.Identity?.IsAuthenticated == true)
    {
        <p class="lede">
            You are already signed in as <strong>@HttpContext.User.Identity?.Name</strong>.
        </p>
        <p><a href="/">Back to the home page</a></p>
    }
    else
    {
        @if (_errorMessage is not null)
        {
            <p class="status-error" role="alert">@_errorMessage</p>
        }

        <EditForm EditContext="_editContext" method="post" OnSubmit="SignInUserAsync" FormName="sign-in">
            <DataAnnotationsValidator />

            <div class="form-field">
                <label for="username">Username</label>
                <InputText id="username" @bind-Value="Input.Username" autocomplete="username webauthn"
                           autocapitalize="none" spellcheck="false" autofocus />
                <ValidationMessage For="@(() => Input.Username)" />
            </div>

            <div class="form-field">
                <label for="password">Password</label>
                <InputText id="password" type="password" @bind-Value="Input.Password"
                           autocomplete="current-password" />
                <ValidationMessage For="@(() => Input.Password)" />
            </div>

            <div class="form-actions">
                <button type="submit" class="button-primary">Sign in</button>
            </div>

            <div class="sign-in-alternative">
                <span class="sign-in-or">or</span>
                <PasskeySubmit Operation="PasskeyOperation.Request" Name="Input.Passkey"
                               EmailName="Input.Username" class="button-secondary">
                    Sign in with a passkey
                </PasskeySubmit>
            </div>
        </EditForm>

        <p class="form-footnote">
            Guests register at the table by scanning its display — there is no stand-alone
            registration page. Lost access? Ask at the counter.
        </p>
    }
</section>

@code {
    private string? _errorMessage;
    private EditContext _editContext = default!;

    [CascadingParameter]
    private HttpContext HttpContext { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm]
    private SignInInputModel Input { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery]
    private string? ReturnUrl { get; set; }

    // BL0008: on a static-SSR form POST the framework binds [SupplyParameterFromForm] itself and may
    // assign null, silently discarding a `= new()` initializer — so the default is applied here instead.
    // OnSubmit means we validate by hand (below), so we drive an explicit EditContext.
    protected override void OnInitialized()
    {
        Input ??= new();
        _editContext = new EditContext(Input);
    }

    private async Task SignInUserAsync()
    {
        string destination = ObligationsEnforcement.SafeLocalReturnUrl(ReturnUrl);

        // Passkey path (§3.3): the element posted an assertion credential (or an error). Handle it
        // before any password validation — the username/password fields are irrelevant here — and
        // note PasskeySignInAsync never returns RequiresTwoFactor (a passkey bypasses the §3.5 second
        // factor by construction).
        if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(Input.Passkey?.Error))
        {
            _errorMessage = "That passkey could not be used. Try again, or sign in with your password.";
            return;
        }

        if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(Input.Passkey?.CredentialJson))
        {
            SignInResult passkeyResult = await SignInManager.PasskeySignInAsync(Input.Passkey.CredentialJson);

            if (passkeyResult.Succeeded)
            {
                Navigation.NavigateTo(destination);
            }
            else if (passkeyResult.IsLockedOut)
            {
                _errorMessage = "Too many failed attempts. The account is locked for about five minutes — try again then.";
            }
            else if (passkeyResult.IsNotAllowed)
            {
                _errorMessage = "This account has been deactivated. Ask at the counter if you think that is a mistake.";
            }
            else
            {
                _errorMessage = "That passkey did not work. Try again, or sign in with your password.";
            }

            return;
        }

        // Password path: OnSubmit fires regardless of validity, so enforce the DataAnnotations now.
        if (!_editContext.Validate())
        {
            return;
        }

        // isPersistent: the §3.1 session is a 24-hour sliding cookie either way; persisting it lets
        // a guest's phone survive a browser restart mid-meal. lockoutOnFailure per §3.1.
        SignInResult result = await SignInManager.PasswordSignInAsync(
            Input.Username,
            Input.Password,
            isPersistent: true,
            lockoutOnFailure: true);

        if (result.Succeeded)
        {
            // The obligations middleware intercepts this navigation when a §3.5 flag is set.
            Navigation.NavigateTo(destination);
        }
        else if (result.RequiresTwoFactor)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo(
                $"{AccountRoutes.SignInTwoFactor}?ReturnUrl={Uri.EscapeDataString(destination)}");
        }
        else if (result.IsLockedOut)
        {
            _errorMessage = "Too many failed attempts. The account is locked for about five minutes — try again then.";
        }
        else if (result.IsNotAllowed)
        {
            _errorMessage = "This account has been deactivated. Ask at the counter if you think that is a mistake.";
        }
        else
        {
            _errorMessage = "That username and password combination did not work.";
        }
    }

    private sealed class SignInInputModel
    {
        [Required(ErrorMessage = "Enter your username.")]
        public string Username { get; set; } = string.Empty;

        [Required(ErrorMessage = "Enter your password.")]
        public string Password { get; set; } = string.Empty;

        // Populated by the passkey-submit element on the assertion path; ignored by the password path.
        // Not [Required] — the passkey button must submit without a username or password.
        public PasskeyInputModel? Passkey { get; set; }
    }
}

@page "/sign-in/two-factor"
@attribute [ExcludeFromInteractiveRouting]
@inject SignInManager<Person> SignInManager
@inject NavigationManager Navigation

@* The TOTP challenge on the password path (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §3.4, §4.2, ADR-0010). Reachable
   only mid-sign-in: the password step parked the pending user in the two-factor cookie; without it
   this page bounces back to /sign-in. There is deliberately no "remember this device" — TOTP is
   challenged on every password sign-in of an enrolled account. The passkey path never lands here. *@

<PageTitle>Two-factor code</PageTitle>

    <p class="eyebrow">MyRestaurant</p>

                       inputmode="numeric" autofocus />
            <ValidationMessage For="@(() => Input.Code)" />

        </div>

        Authenticator unavailable?
        <a href="@RecoveryCodeHref">Use a recovery code instead.</a>
    </p>
</section>

@code {
    private string? _errorMessage;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm]
    private TwoFactorInputModel Input { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery]
    private string? ReturnUrl { get; set; }

    private string RecoveryCodeHref
        => $"{AccountRoutes.SignInRecoveryCode}?ReturnUrl={Uri.EscapeDataString(ObligationsEnforcement.SafeLocalReturnUrl(ReturnUrl))}";

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
    {
        // BL0008: a form POST binds Input itself and may assign null, so the default lives here
        // rather than in a property initializer the binder would silently discard.
        Input ??= new();

        // No pending two-factor user means this page was reached out of order — start over.
        if (await SignInManager.GetTwoFactorAuthenticationUserAsync() is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo(AccountRoutes.SignIn);
        }
    }

    private async Task VerifyCodeAsync()
    {
        if (await SignInManager.GetTwoFactorAuthenticationUserAsync() is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo(AccountRoutes.SignIn);
            return;
        }

        // Authenticator apps display codes in groups; be forgiving about spaces and dashes.
        string code = Input.Code.Replace(" ", string.Empty).Replace("-", string.Empty);

        SignInResult result = await SignInManager.TwoFactorAuthenticatorSignInAsync(
            code,
            isPersistent: true,
            rememberClient: false);

        if (result.Succeeded)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo(ObligationsEnforcement.SafeLocalReturnUrl(ReturnUrl));
        }
        else if (result.IsLockedOut)
        {
            _errorMessage = "Too many failed attempts. The account is locked for about five minutes — try again then.";
        }
        else
        {
            _errorMessage = "That code did not verify. Codes rotate every 30 seconds — check the app and try the current one.";
        }
    }

    private sealed class TwoFactorInputModel
    {
        [Required(ErrorMessage = "Enter the six-digit code.")]
        public string Code { get; set; } = string.Empty;
    }
}

@using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Antiforgery
@using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection
@inject IServiceProvider Services

@*
    Renders the passkey button plus the form-associated <passkey-submit> custom element (passkey.js).
    The element needs an antiforgery token it can send as a request header on its fetch() to the
    ceremony endpoints (those endpoints are not form posts, so the token cannot ride along in form
    data); we resolve it here from IAntiforgery and hand it over via attributes. Adapted from the
    ASP.NET Core Blazor Web template's PasskeySubmit component.

<passkey-submit
    operation="@Operation"
    name="@Name"
    email-name="@EmailName"
    creation-options-url="@CreationOptionsUrl"
    request-options-url="@RequestOptionsUrl"
    request-token-name="@_tokens?.HeaderName"
    request-token-value="@_tokens?.RequestToken">
</passkey-submit>

    [Parameter]

    /// the setup wizard only registers passkeys, so it does not set this.

    [Parameter]

@using System.Globalization
@using MyRestaurant.Domain.Time
@inject IClock Clock
@inject RestaurantTime RestaurantClock

@* The restaurant wall clock (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §11.7). On every page, in both layouts.

   Every instant this application shows is rendered in RESTAURANT_TIME_ZONE and never in the reader's
   own zone (§8.1) — which is the right rule and an invisible one. A guest reading "sent 3:04 PM" from
   another continent has no way to know whose three o'clock that is unless the page says so, standing
   somewhere they will look. This footer is that statement, and it earns its place by also being useful
   to the people in the building: one authoritative clock, the same on the counter's screen, the
   kitchen's, and the tablet on table four.

   TICKING WITHOUT A TIMER. There is deliberately no server-side timer here. A Blazor timer would tick
   only on interactive pages (half the surfaces here are static SSR), would cost one render and one
   circuit message per second per open tab, and would keep a phone's radio awake to do it. Instead the
   component renders one anchor — the instant, the zone offset that applies to it, and when that offset
   next changes — and js/clock.js advances it locally against a monotonic clock, pausing entirely while
   the tab is hidden. The server is asked again on a page load, and thereafter only rarely (§11.7).

   ShouldRender is pinned false for the same reason: once the anchor is in the DOM the script owns that
   text node, and a re-render from the framework would fight it. Nothing about this component depends on
   state that changes, so there is nothing to lose by never rendering twice. *@

<footer class="app-footer">
    <p class="restaurant-clock"
       id="@ElementId"
       data-epoch-milliseconds="@_epochMilliseconds"
       data-utc-offset-minutes="@_utcOffsetMinutes"
       data-next-transition-epoch-milliseconds="@_nextTransitionEpochMilliseconds"
       data-next-utc-offset-minutes="@_nextUtcOffsetMinutes"
       data-twelve-hour-clock="@_twelveHourClock"
       data-snapshot-url="@RestaurantClockRoutes.Snapshot">
        <span class="restaurant-clock-label">Restaurant time</span>
        <time class="restaurant-clock-reading"
              data-restaurant-clock-reading="true"
              datetime="@_machineReadable">@_reading</time>
        <span class="restaurant-clock-zone" title="@_zoneIdentifier">@_zoneLabel</span>
    </p>
</footer>

@code {
    /// <summary>The element js/clock.js looks for. Exactly one per document.</summary>
    public const string ElementId = "restaurant-clock";

    private string _epochMilliseconds = string.Empty;
    private string _utcOffsetMinutes = string.Empty;
    private string _nextTransitionEpochMilliseconds = string.Empty;
    private string _nextUtcOffsetMinutes = string.Empty;
    private string _twelveHourClock = "true";
    private string _machineReadable = string.Empty;
    private string _reading = string.Empty;
    private string _zoneLabel = string.Empty;
    private string _zoneIdentifier = string.Empty;

    protected override void OnInitialized()
    {
        // One instant for the whole component, so the rendered text and the anchor the script starts
        // from cannot disagree by the microseconds between two reads of the clock.
        DateTimeOffset now = Clock.UtcNow;
        RestaurantClockSnapshot snapshot = RestaurantClock.Snapshot(now);

        // Every attribute is formatted invariantly rather than left to the ambient culture: these are
        // numbers a script parses, not text a person reads, and a culture that groups digits or writes
        // a different minus sign would hand js/clock.js something it cannot parse.
        _epochMilliseconds = snapshot.EpochMilliseconds.ToString(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture);
        _utcOffsetMinutes = snapshot.UtcOffsetMinutes.ToString(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture);
        _nextTransitionEpochMilliseconds =
            snapshot.NextTransitionEpochMilliseconds?.ToString(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture) ?? string.Empty;
        _nextUtcOffsetMinutes =
            snapshot.NextUtcOffsetMinutes?.ToString(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture) ?? string.Empty;
        _twelveHourClock = snapshot.UsesTwelveHourClock ? "true" : "false";

        _reading = RestaurantClock.DateAndTimeWithSeconds(now);
        _machineReadable = RestaurantClock.MachineReadable(now);
        _zoneLabel = snapshot.ZoneLabel;
        _zoneIdentifier = snapshot.ZoneIdentifier;
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// Never re-render. The script owns this subtree after the first paint; a framework re-render would
    /// overwrite a correct ticking reading with a stale one and reset the script's anchor for nothing.
    /// </summary>
    protected override bool ShouldRender() => false;
}

@code {
    private bool _created;
    private string? _createdUsername;
    private Guid _createdPersonIdentifier;
    private string? _temporaryPassword;
    private string? _grantedRolesText;
    private string? _errorMessage;

    [CascadingParameter]
    private HttpContext HttpContext { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm(FormName = "create-staff")]
    private CreateStaffInputModel Input { get; set; } = default!;

    protected override void OnInitialized()
        // BL0008: a form POST binds Input itself and may assign null, so the default lives here.
        => Input ??= new();

    private async Task CreateAsync()
    {
        Person? actingAdministrator = await UserManager.GetUserAsync(HttpContext.User);
        if (actingAdministrator is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo(AccountRoutes.SignIn);
            return;
        }

        string username = Input.Username.Trim();
        string? displayName = string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(Input.DisplayName) ? null : Input.DisplayName.Trim();

        // Best-effort duplicate check; the person UNIQUE constraint inside the transaction is authoritative.
        if (await UserManager.FindByNameAsync(username) is not null)
        {
            _errorMessage = "That username is already taken. Please choose another.";
            return;
        }

        List<string> roles = [];
        if (Input.GrantAdministrator)
        {
            roles.Add(RestaurantRoles.Administrator);
        }

        if (Input.GrantCounter)
        {
            roles.Add(RestaurantRoles.Counter);
        }

        if (Input.GrantKitchen)
        {
            roles.Add(RestaurantRoles.Kitchen);
        }

        Guid personIdentifier = IdentifierFactory.Create();

        // A generated temporary password, hashed immediately so the plaintext is only ever held for the
        // one response that shows it. 12 random bytes render to a 16-character URL-safe string — well
        // over the 12-character policy floor (§3.2), which the forced change re-checks anyway.
        string temporaryPassword = SecretGenerator.GenerateBase64UrlSecret(12);
        string passwordHash = PasswordHasher.HashPassword(
            new Person { PersonIdentifier = personIdentifier, Username = username },
            temporaryPassword);

        CreateStaffStatus status = await Accounts.CreateStaffAsync(
            new NewStaffAccount(personIdentifier, username, displayName, passwordHash, roles),
            actingAdministrator.PersonIdentifier,
            HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        if (status == CreateStaffStatus.UsernameTaken)
        {
            _errorMessage = "That username was taken while you were filling this in. Please choose another.";
            return;
        }

        _createdUsername = username;
        _createdPersonIdentifier = personIdentifier;
        _temporaryPassword = temporaryPassword;
        _grantedRolesText = FormatRoles(roles);
        _created = true;
    }

    private static string? FormatRoles(IReadOnlyList<string> roles) => roles.Count switch
    {
        0 => null,
        1 => roles[0],
        _ => $"{string.Join(", ", roles.Take(roles.Count - 1))} and {roles[^1]}",
    };

    private sealed class CreateStaffInputModel
    {
        [Required(ErrorMessage = "Choose a username.")]
        [StringLength(64, MinimumLength = 3, ErrorMessage = "The username must be 3–64 characters.")]
        public string Username { get; set; } = string.Empty;

        [StringLength(120, ErrorMessage = "That display name is too long.")]
        public string? DisplayName { get; set; }

        public bool GrantAdministrator { get; set; }

        public bool GrantCounter { get; set; }

        public bool GrantKitchen { get; set; }
    }
}

@code {
    private bool _created;
    private string? _createdLabel;
    private Guid _createdTableIdentifier;
    private string? _errorMessage;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm(FormName = "create-table")]
    private CreateTableInputModel Input { get; set; } = default!;

    protected override void OnInitialized()
        // BL0008: a form POST binds Input itself and may assign null, so the default lives here.
        => Input ??= new();

    private async Task CreateAsync()
    {
        string label = Input.Label.Trim();
        Guid tableIdentifier = IdentifierFactory.Create();

        CreateTableOutcome outcome = await Tables.CreateTableAsync(
            tableIdentifier, label, HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        switch (outcome)
        {
            case CreateTableOutcome.Created:
                _createdLabel = label;
                _createdTableIdentifier = tableIdentifier;
                _created = true;
                break;
            case CreateTableOutcome.LabelTaken:
                _errorMessage = "That label is already used by another table. Please choose a different one.";
                break;
        }
    }

    [CascadingParameter]
    private HttpContext HttpContext { get; set; } = default!;

    private sealed class CreateTableInputModel
    {
        [Required(ErrorMessage = "Choose a label for the table.")]
        [StringLength(64, MinimumLength = 1, ErrorMessage = "The label must be 1–64 characters.")]
        public string Label { get; set; } = string.Empty;
    }
}

        text-transform: capitalize;

    .chip-ok {

@code {
    private static readonly string[] AllStaffRoles =
        [RestaurantRoles.Administrator, RestaurantRoles.Counter, RestaurantRoles.Kitchen];

    private PersonSummary? _person;
    private IReadOnlyList<string> _grantableRoles = [];
    private bool _isSelf;
    private string? _flashMessage;
    private string? _errorMessage;

    private CredentialResetResult? _resetResult;
    private string? _temporaryPassword;

    [Parameter]
    public Guid PersonId { get; set; }

    [CascadingParameter]
    private HttpContext HttpContext { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm(FormName = "manage-grant-role")]
    private RoleSelectionModel GrantInput { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm(FormName = "manage-revoke-role")]
    private RoleSelectionModel RevokeInput { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery]
    private string? Done { get; set; }

    private string ManagePath => $"/administration/people/{PersonId}";

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
    {
        // BL0008: form POSTs bind these themselves and may assign null, so defaults live here.
        GrantInput ??= new();
        RevokeInput ??= new();

        _person = await People.GetPersonAsync(PersonId, HttpContext.RequestAborted);
        if (_person is null)
        {
            return;
        }

        _grantableRoles = AllStaffRoles.Where(role => !_person.Roles.Contains(role)).ToArray();

        Person? actingAdministrator = await UserManager.GetUserAsync(HttpContext.User);
        _isSelf = actingAdministrator is not null && actingAdministrator.PersonIdentifier == _person.PersonIdentifier;

        // Render the flash for a completed action after the post/redirect/get, on GET only.
        if (HttpContext.Request.Method == HttpMethods.Get)
        {
            _flashMessage = FlashFor(Done);
        }
    }

    private async Task GrantRoleAsync()
    {
        if (_person is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo("/administration");
            return;
        }

        Person? admin = await UserManager.GetUserAsync(HttpContext.User);
        if (admin is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo(AccountRoutes.SignIn);
            return;
        }

        if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(GrantInput.RoleName))
        {
            _errorMessage = "Choose a role to grant.";
            return;
        }

        RoleGrantOutcome outcome = await Accounts.GrantRoleAsync(
            _person.PersonIdentifier, GrantInput.RoleName, admin.PersonIdentifier, HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        switch (outcome)
        {
            case RoleGrantOutcome.Granted:
                RedirectWithOutcome("role-granted");
                break;
            case RoleGrantOutcome.AlreadyHeld:
                RedirectWithOutcome("role-already-held");
                break;
            case RoleGrantOutcome.PersonNotFound:
                Navigation.NavigateTo(ManagePath);
                break;
        }
    }

    private async Task RevokeRoleAsync()
    {
        if (_person is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo("/administration");
            return;
        }

        Person? admin = await UserManager.GetUserAsync(HttpContext.User);
        if (admin is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo(AccountRoutes.SignIn);
            return;
        }

        if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(RevokeInput.RoleName))
        {
            _errorMessage = "Choose a role to revoke.";
            return;
        }

        RoleRevokeOutcome outcome = await Accounts.RevokeRoleAsync(
            _person.PersonIdentifier, RevokeInput.RoleName, admin.PersonIdentifier, HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        switch (outcome)
        {
            case RoleRevokeOutcome.Revoked:
                RedirectWithOutcome("role-revoked");
                break;
            case RoleRevokeOutcome.NotHeld:
                RedirectWithOutcome("role-not-held");
                break;
            case RoleRevokeOutcome.WouldRemoveLastAdministrator:
                _errorMessage = "This is the only administrator, so the administrator role cannot be removed. "
                    + "Grant administrator to someone else first.";
                break;
            case RoleRevokeOutcome.PersonNotFound:
                Navigation.NavigateTo(ManagePath);
                break;
        }
    }

    private async Task ResetCredentialsAsync()
    {
        if (_person is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo("/administration");
            return;
        }

        Person? admin = await UserManager.GetUserAsync(HttpContext.User);
        if (admin is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo(AccountRoutes.SignIn);
            return;
        }

        // Generate + hash the temporary password here so the plaintext is only ever held for the one
        // response that shows it (§3.2). 12 random bytes → a 16-character URL-safe string.
        string temporaryPassword = SecretGenerator.GenerateBase64UrlSecret(12);
        string passwordHash = PasswordHasher.HashPassword(
            new Person { PersonIdentifier = _person.PersonIdentifier, Username = _person.Username },
            temporaryPassword);

        CredentialResetResult result = await Accounts.ResetCredentialsAsync(
            _person.PersonIdentifier, passwordHash, admin.PersonIdentifier, HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        if (result.Outcome == CredentialResetOutcome.PersonNotFound)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo(ManagePath);
            return;
        }

        // Show the temporary password once, in this response (no redirect).
        _temporaryPassword = temporaryPassword;
        _resetResult = result;
    }

    private async Task ToggleActivationAsync()
    {
        if (_person is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo("/administration");
            return;
        }

        Person? admin = await UserManager.GetUserAsync(HttpContext.User);
        if (admin is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo(AccountRoutes.SignIn);
            return;
        }

        bool target = !_person.IsActive;
        AccountActivationOutcome outcome = await Accounts.SetAccountActiveAsync(
            _person.PersonIdentifier, target, admin.PersonIdentifier, HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        switch (outcome)
        {
            case AccountActivationOutcome.Changed:
                RedirectWithOutcome(target ? "account-reactivated" : "account-deactivated");
                break;
            case AccountActivationOutcome.NoChange:
                Navigation.NavigateTo(ManagePath);
                break;
            case AccountActivationOutcome.WouldDeactivateLastAdministrator:
                _errorMessage = "This is the only administrator that can sign in, so it cannot be deactivated. "
                    + "Make sure another administrator is active first.";
                break;
            case AccountActivationOutcome.PersonNotFound:
                Navigation.NavigateTo(ManagePath);
                break;
        }
    }

    private void RedirectWithOutcome(string outcome)
        => Navigation.NavigateTo($"{ManagePath}?done={outcome}");

    private static string? FlashFor(string? outcome) => outcome switch
    {
        "role-granted" => "Role granted. It takes effect on their sessions within a few minutes.",
        "role-already-held" => "That role was already held — nothing changed.",
        "role-revoked" => "Role revoked. It takes effect on their sessions within a few minutes.",
        "role-not-held" => "That role was not held — nothing changed.",
        "account-deactivated" => "Account deactivated. Its sessions end within a few minutes.",
        "account-reactivated" => "Account reactivated.",
        _ => null,
    };

    private bool IsLockedOut(PersonSummary person)
        => person.LockoutEndAt is { } end && end > Clock.UtcNow;

    private static string Capitalize(string role)
        => string.IsNullOrEmpty(role) ? role : char.ToUpperInvariant(role[0]) + role[1..];

    private sealed class RoleSelectionModel
    {
        public string RoleName { get; set; } = string.Empty;
    }
}

@code {
    private RestaurantTableSummary? _table;
    private string? _flashMessage;
    private string? _errorMessage;

    [Parameter]
    public Guid TableId { get; set; }

    [CascadingParameter]
    private HttpContext HttpContext { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm(FormName = "manage-rename")]
    private RenameInputModel RenameInput { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery]
    private string? Done { get; set; }

    private string ManagePath => $"/administration/tables/{TableId}";

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
    {
        // BL0008: a form POST binds RenameInput itself and may assign null, so the default lives here.
        RenameInput ??= new();

        _table = await TableDirectory.GetTableAsync(TableId, HttpContext.RequestAborted);
        if (_table is null)
        {
            return;
        }

        // On GET, pre-fill the rename box with the current label and render any post/redirect flash.
        // On POST the submitted value is already bound, so it must not be overwritten.
        if (HttpContext.Request.Method == HttpMethods.Get)
        {
            if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(RenameInput.Label))
            {
                RenameInput.Label = _table.Label;
            }

            _flashMessage = FlashFor(Done);
        }
    }

    private async Task RenameAsync()
    {
        if (_table is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo("/administration/tables");
            return;
        }

        RenameTableOutcome outcome = await Tables.RenameTableAsync(
            TableId, RenameInput.Label.Trim(), HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        switch (outcome)
        {
            case RenameTableOutcome.Renamed:
                RedirectWithOutcome("renamed");
                break;
            case RenameTableOutcome.NoChange:
                RedirectWithOutcome("rename-no-change");
                break;
            case RenameTableOutcome.LabelTaken:
                _errorMessage = "Another table already uses that label. Please choose a different one.";
                break;
            case RenameTableOutcome.TableNotFound:
                Navigation.NavigateTo("/administration/tables");
                break;
        }
    }

    private async Task RotateSecretAsync()
    {
        if (_table is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo("/administration/tables");
            return;
        }

        RotateJoinSecretOutcome outcome = await Tables.RotateJoinSecretAsync(TableId, HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        switch (outcome)
        {
            case RotateJoinSecretOutcome.Rotated:
                RedirectWithOutcome("secret-rotated");
                break;
            case RotateJoinSecretOutcome.TableNotFound:
                Navigation.NavigateTo("/administration/tables");
                break;
        }
    }

    private async Task ToggleActivationAsync()
    {
        if (_table is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo("/administration/tables");
            return;
        }

        bool target = !_table.IsActive;
        TableActivationOutcome outcome = await Tables.SetTableActiveAsync(TableId, target, HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        switch (outcome)
        {
            case TableActivationOutcome.Changed:
                RedirectWithOutcome(target ? "reactivated" : "deactivated");
                break;
            case TableActivationOutcome.NoChange:
                Navigation.NavigateTo(ManagePath);
                break;
            case TableActivationOutcome.TableNotFound:
                Navigation.NavigateTo("/administration/tables");
                break;
        }
    }

    private void RedirectWithOutcome(string outcome)
        => Navigation.NavigateTo($"{ManagePath}?done={outcome}");

    private static string? FlashFor(string? outcome) => outcome switch
    {
        "renamed" => "Table renamed.",
        "rename-no-change" => "That was already the label — nothing changed.",
        "secret-rotated" => "Join secret rotated. Every outstanding QR for this table has stopped working; "
            + "paired displays pick up the new one automatically.",
        "deactivated" => "Table deactivated. Its join tokens no longer validate and its display stops rendering.",
        "reactivated" => "Table reactivated.",
        _ => null,
    };

    private sealed class RenameInputModel
    {
        [Required(ErrorMessage = "Enter a label.")]
        [StringLength(64, MinimumLength = 1, ErrorMessage = "The label must be 1–64 characters.")]
        public string Label { get; set; } = string.Empty;
    }
}

@page "/administration/tables/{TableId:guid}/displays"

@* Display devices for one table (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §4.2, §11.4 — `area.administration`).
   Static SSR, like every administration surface.

   Generate deliberately does NOT post/redirect/get: the plaintext code exists exactly once, in the
   response to the POST that made it, and a redirect would throw it away — the same reason the TOTP
   slice renders recovery codes in place. A refresh therefore mints a fresh code; the previous one is
   simply left to expire, which is harmless because codes are single-use and short-lived.

   Revoke does use post/redirect/get, and picks its device from a select rather than rendering a form
   per row — the same shape ManagePerson uses for role revocation, and the reason is the same: one
   named form per action keeps static-SSR form matching unambiguous. *@

        <h2 class="manage-heading">Pair a new display</h2>

        {
            <p class="lede">
                Generate a one-time code, then open <code>@PairingUrl</code> on the tablet and type it in.
                Codes last @Options.TableDisplayPairingCodeMinutes
                minute@(Options.TableDisplayPairingCodeMinutes == 1 ? "" : "s"), work once, and the
                pairing page is rate-limited to @DisplayRoutes.PairingAttemptsPerWindow attempts a minute

                Reactivate it first.
            </p>
        }

        <hr class="manage-rule" />

        <h2 class="manage-heading">Paired displays</h2>
        @if (_devices.Count == 0)

@code {
    private RestaurantTableSummary? _table;
    private IReadOnlyList<TableDisplayDeviceSummary> _devices = [];
    private IReadOnlyList<TableDisplayDeviceSummary> _revocableDevices = [];
    private string? _issuedCode;
    private DateTimeOffset? _issuedExpiresAt;
    private string? _flashMessage;
    private string? _errorMessage;

    [Parameter]
    public Guid TableId { get; set; }

    [CascadingParameter]
    private HttpContext HttpContext { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm(FormName = "display-revoke")]
    private RevokeInputModel RevokeInput { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery]
    private string? Done { get; set; }

    private string ManagePath => $"/administration/tables/{TableId}";

    private string DisplaysPath => $"/administration/tables/{TableId}/displays";

    /// <summary>The absolute URL to read aloud to whoever is holding the tablet (§4.2).</summary>
    private string PairingUrl => $"{Options.PublicOrigin.TrimEnd('/')}{DisplayRoutes.Pair}";

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
    {
        // BL0008: a form POST binds RevokeInput itself and may assign null, so the default lives here.
        RevokeInput ??= new();

        _table = await TableDirectory.GetTableAsync(TableId, HttpContext.RequestAborted);
        if (_table is null)
        {
            return;
        }

        await LoadDevicesAsync();

        if (HttpMethods.IsGet(HttpContext.Request.Method))
        {
            _flashMessage = FlashFor(Done);
        }
    }

    private async Task LoadDevicesAsync()
    {
        _devices = await DisplayDevices.ListDevicesForTableAsync(TableId, HttpContext.RequestAborted);
        _revocableDevices = _devices.Where(device => !device.IsRevoked).ToArray();
    }

    private async Task GenerateCodeAsync()
    {
        if (_table is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo("/administration/tables");
            return;
        }

        if (PersonPrincipal.IdentifierFor(HttpContext.User) is not { } administrator)
        {
            // Endpoint authorization already guarantees an administrator; this is the belt to that
            // brace, because created_by_person_identifier is NOT NULL and has no anonymous option.
            _errorMessage = "Your session could not be identified. Sign in again and retry.";
            return;
        }

        IssuePairingCodeResult result = await Pairing.IssuePairingCodeAsync(
            TableId,
            administrator,
            TimeSpan.FromMinutes(Options.TableDisplayPairingCodeMinutes),
            HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        if (result.Outcome == IssuePairingCodeOutcome.Issued)
        {
            // Rendered in place, never redirected: this is the only moment the plaintext exists.
            _issuedCode = result.Code;
            _issuedExpiresAt = result.ExpiresAt;
            return;
        }

        _errorMessage = "This table is deactivated, so it cannot take a new display. Reactivate it first.";
    }

    private async Task RevokeDeviceAsync()
    {
        if (_table is null)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo("/administration/tables");
            return;
        }

        // Bound as text rather than Guid so the "Choose a display…" empty option is representable and
        // InputSelect never has to parse a non-string type.
        if (!Guid.TryParse(RevokeInput.DeviceIdentifier, out Guid deviceIdentifier))
        {
            _errorMessage = "Choose which display to revoke.";
            return;
        }

        if (PersonPrincipal.IdentifierFor(HttpContext.User) is not { } administrator)
        {
            _errorMessage = "Your session could not be identified. Sign in again and retry.";
            return;
        }

        RevokeDisplayDeviceOutcome outcome = await Pairing.RevokeDeviceAsync(
            deviceIdentifier, administrator, HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        switch (outcome)
        {
            case RevokeDisplayDeviceOutcome.Revoked:
                Navigation.NavigateTo($"{DisplaysPath}?done=revoked");
                break;
            case RevokeDisplayDeviceOutcome.AlreadyRevoked:
                Navigation.NavigateTo($"{DisplaysPath}?done=already-revoked");
                break;
            case RevokeDisplayDeviceOutcome.DeviceNotFound:
                _errorMessage = "That display no longer exists.";
                await LoadDevicesAsync();
                break;
        }
    }

    private static string? FlashFor(string? outcome) => outcome switch
    {
        "revoked" => "Display revoked. Its credential stops working on the device's next request.",
        "already-revoked" => "That display had already been revoked — nothing changed.",
        _ => null,
    };

    private sealed class RevokeInputModel
    {
        [Required(ErrorMessage = "Choose which display to revoke.")]
        public string DeviceIdentifier { get; set; } = string.Empty;
    }
}

@page "/display/pair"
@using Microsoft.AspNetCore.RateLimiting
@using MyRestaurant.DataAccess.Displays
@using MyRestaurant.WebApplication.Displays
@attribute [ExcludeFromInteractiveRouting]
@attribute [EnableRateLimiting(DisplayRoutes.PairingRateLimitPolicy)]
@layout DisplayLayout
@inject IDisplayDevicePairing Pairing
@inject RestaurantOptions Options
@inject NavigationManager Navigation

@* Display-device pairing (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §4.2, §11.5).

   Anonymous by necessity: this is the one page an unpaired screen can reach, and it is what it reaches
   INSTEAD of a sign-in page — a tablet has no account and never will. §4.2 pays for that openness with a
   rate limit rather than a credential: 5 attempts per minute per IP, enforced by the policy named in the
   attribute above, so an attacker cannot walk the 31^8 code space and a fat-fingered member of staff is
   barely inconvenienced.

   Static SSR, like every surface that writes a cookie: pairing's last act is to set the year-long device
   credential, which a Blazor circuit cannot do.

   Three entry states, decided on GET:
     • already paired  — the middleware resolved a live credential; offer the display, do not re-pair.
     • disconnected    — a cookie was presented but not honoured, so the middleware cleared it. §11.5
                         asks for exactly this wording; revoked and mangled look the same, on purpose.
     • fresh           — no cookie at all; just the form.

   Failures are indistinguishable by design. Unknown, expired, already-used, and malformed codes all
   produce one sentence, because anything finer turns an anonymous endpoint into an oracle for which
   codes exist (§4.2: "failed attempts burn nothing but the rate budget"). *@

<PageTitle>Pair this display</PageTitle>

<section class="display-card">
    <p class="display-eyebrow">@Options.RestaurantName</p>

    @if (_pairedTable is { } pairedTable)
    {
        <h1>This display is paired</h1>
        <p class="display-lede">
            It is already showing <strong>@(_pairedTableLabel ?? "a table")</strong>. There is nothing to
            do here — open the display, or ask an administrator to revoke this device first if it needs
            to move to another table.
        </p>
        <div class="form-actions display-actions">
            <a class="button-primary" href="@DisplayRoutes.ForTable(pairedTable)">Open the display</a>
        </div>
    }
    else
    {
        <h1>Pair this display</h1>

        @if (_wasDisconnected)
        {
            <p class="status-error" role="alert">
                This display was disconnected. Ask an administrator for a new pairing code to bring it
                back.
            </p>
        }

        <p class="display-lede">
            An administrator generates a one-time code from Administration → Tables → the table →
            <strong>Display devices</strong>. Type it in below. Codes last
            @Options.TableDisplayPairingCodeMinutes
            minute@(Options.TableDisplayPairingCodeMinutes == 1 ? "" : "s") and work once.
        </p>

        @if (_errorMessage is not null)
        {
            <p class="status-error" role="alert">@_errorMessage</p>
        }

        <EditForm Model="PairInput" method="post" OnValidSubmit="PairAsync" FormName="display-pair" class="display-form">
            <DataAnnotationsValidator />

            <div class="form-field">
                <label for="pairing-code">Pairing code</label>
                <InputText id="pairing-code" class="pairing-code-input" @bind-Value="PairInput.Code"
                           autocomplete="off" autocapitalize="characters" autocorrect="off"
                           spellcheck="false" inputmode="text" maxlength="32" />
                <ValidationMessage For="@(() => PairInput.Code)" />

                           placeholder="Window tablet" autocomplete="off" maxlength="120" />

            </div>
        </EditForm>

            Pairing stores a long-lived credential on this device. If the tablet is lost or replaced, an
            administrator revokes it and the credential dies on its next request — the table's join
            secret never leaves the server, so the screen itself holds nothing worth taking.
        </p>
    }
</section>

@code {
    private string? _errorMessage;
    private bool _wasDisconnected;
    private Guid? _pairedTable;
    private string? _pairedTableLabel;

    [CascadingParameter]
    private HttpContext HttpContext { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm(FormName = "display-pair")]
    private PairInputModel PairInput { get; set; } = default!;

    protected override void OnInitialized()
    {
        // BL0008: a form POST binds PairInput itself and may assign null, so the default lives here.
        PairInput ??= new();

        // The middleware has already run, so a live credential is visible as the request's principal and
        // a dead one has already been cleared from the response — but the request's own copy is still
        // readable, which is how "disconnected" is told apart from "never paired" (§11.5).
        _pairedTable = DisplayDevicePrincipal.TableIdentifierFor(HttpContext.User);
        _pairedTableLabel = DisplayDevicePrincipal.TableLabelFor(HttpContext.User);
        _wasDisconnected = _pairedTable is null && DisplayDeviceCookie.WasPresented(HttpContext.Request);
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// Redeems the typed code. Normalization (case, spaces, hyphens) happens inside the service, so what
    /// a person read off one screen and typed into another does not have to match byte for byte.
    /// </summary>
    private async Task PairAsync()
    {
        RedeemPairingCodeResult result = await Pairing.RedeemPairingCodeAsync(
            PairInput.Code, PairInput.DeviceLabel, HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        if (result.Outcome == RedeemPairingCodeOutcome.Paired
            && result.DeviceIdentifier is { } device
            && result.TableIdentifier is { } table
            && result.DeviceSecret is { } secret)
        {
            // The secret exists in memory exactly once, here: only its SHA-256 hash was stored (§4.2).
            DisplayDeviceCookie.Write(HttpContext.Response, device, secret);
            Navigation.NavigateTo(DisplayRoutes.ForTable(table));
            return;
        }

        // One wording for every refusal. A deactivated table, an expired code, a used code and a typo
        // must be indistinguishable from out here (§4.2).
        _errorMessage = "That code was not recognised. Codes work once and expire quickly — ask for a "
            + "fresh one and try again.";
    }

    private sealed class PairInputModel
    {
        [Required(ErrorMessage = "Enter the pairing code.")]
        [StringLength(32, MinimumLength = 8, ErrorMessage = "A pairing code is 8 characters.")]
        public string Code { get; set; } = string.Empty;

        [StringLength(120, ErrorMessage = "Keep the name under 120 characters.")]
        public string? DeviceLabel { get; set; }
    }
}

@page "/display/{TableId:guid}"
@using MyRestaurant.DataAccess.Displays

@implements IDisposable

@inject ISittingDirectory Sittings
@inject IDomainEventBroadcaster Broadcaster
@inject IClock Clock

@* The table display surface (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §4.3, §11.5).

   Interactive server, unlike every other cookie-adjacent page here, because §11.5 asks for three live
   things: a QR that re-renders on the rotation boundary, a party-size chip fed by SittingMemberJoined,
   and a connection state that must never let a frozen code masquerade as a fresh one.

   ANONYMOUS at the endpoint, gated in the component. §11.5 says an unpaired device is *redirected* to
   /display/pair, and [Authorize] cannot produce that: a failed policy challenges the default scheme and
   lands the screen on /sign-in, which is meaningless for a tablet. The device principal itself is
   installed by DisplayDeviceAuthenticationMiddleware and reaches the circuit through the cascading
   authentication state, so the gate below is reading a server-set principal, never anything the browser
   claimed. §3.7's "table claim matches {table}" is a comparison against a route value, which likewise
   belongs in the surface — the same place §3.7 already leaves /table's per-sitting membership check.

   Rotation is continuous and independent of sitting state (§4.3), so the timer runs whether or not the
   table has anyone at it. Deactivating the table stops rendering (§4.1) without unpairing the device. *@

<PageTitle>@PageTitleText</PageTitle>

@if (_stage == DisplayStage.WrongTable && _deviceTable is { } ownTable)

    <section class="display-card">
        <p class="display-eyebrow">@Options.RestaurantName</p>
