@code {
    /// <summary>Which of the §11.5 states this display resolved to.</summary>
    private enum DisplayStage
    {
        /// <summary>No live device credential: §11.5 sends the screen to the pairing surface.</summary>
        NotPaired,

        /// <summary>A live device, but it belongs to a different table (§3.7's table-claim rule).</summary>
        WrongTable,

        /// <summary>Paired and correct, but the table is deactivated — no code renders (§4.1).</summary>
        TableOutOfService,

        /// <summary>Paired, correct, and in service: the rotating QR.</summary>
        Live,
    }

    private DisplayStage _stage = DisplayStage.NotPaired;
    private Guid? _deviceIdentifier;
    private Guid? _deviceTable;
    private string? _deviceTableLabel;
    private string _tableLabel = string.Empty;
    private TableJoinQrCode? _qr;
    private int _partySize;
    private int _refreshSequence;

    // Captured once, so nothing ever touches _lifetime.Token after Dispose has run.
    private readonly CancellationTokenSource _lifetime = new();
    private CancellationToken _stopping;
    private IDisposable? _subscription;
    private bool _disposed;

    [Parameter]
    public Guid TableId { get; set; }

    [CascadingParameter]
    private Task<AuthenticationState>? AuthenticationStateTask { get; set; }

    private string PageTitleText => _stage == DisplayStage.NotPaired
        ? "Pair this display"
        : string.IsNullOrEmpty(_tableLabel) ? "Table display" : _tableLabel;

    /// <summary>
    /// How long a rendered code stays trustworthy, for js/display.js. One rotation covers the healthy
    /// case (the loop refreshes within a fraction of a second of the boundary); the extra ten seconds is
    /// slack for a slow round trip, so a working display never flickers into the offline state.
    /// </summary>
    private int FreshForMilliseconds => (Options.TableJoinTokenRotationSeconds + 10) * 1000;

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
    {
        _stopping = _lifetime.Token;

        if (AuthenticationStateTask is null)
        {
            _stage = DisplayStage.NotPaired;
            return;
        }

        // The cascading authentication state is the circuit-safe way to read the principal: there is no
        // HttpContext once the component is interactive, and it works identically during the prerender
        // pass. The device principal reaches both because the middleware runs on /display AND /_blazor.
        AuthenticationState state = await AuthenticationStateTask;

        _deviceIdentifier = DisplayDevicePrincipal.DeviceIdentifierFor(state.User);
        _deviceTable = DisplayDevicePrincipal.TableIdentifierFor(state.User);
        _deviceTableLabel = DisplayDevicePrincipal.TableLabelFor(state.User);

        if (_deviceIdentifier is null || _deviceTable is null)
        {
            // §11.5: "Unpaired device → redirect /display/pair". During the prerender pass this becomes
            // an HTTP redirect and the circuit never starts; on the circuit it is a navigation. The
            // rendered not-paired card above stands behind it either way.
            _stage = DisplayStage.NotPaired;
            Navigation.NavigateTo(DisplayRoutes.Pair);
            return;
        }

        if (_deviceTable.Value != TableId)
        {
            _stage = DisplayStage.WrongTable;
            return;
        }

        _tableLabel = _deviceTableLabel ?? string.Empty;
        await LoadAsync();
    }

    protected override void OnAfterRender(bool firstRender)
    {
        if (!firstRender || _stage is DisplayStage.NotPaired or DisplayStage.WrongTable)
        {
            return;
        }

        // Only on the circuit: OnAfterRender does not run during prerendering, so neither the timer nor
        // the subscription is ever created for a render that is about to be thrown away.
        _subscription = Broadcaster.Subscribe(OnDomainNotification);
        _ = RunRefreshLoopAsync();
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// Re-reads everything the surface shows. Revalidating the device on every pass is what makes §4.2's
    /// "revocation kills the device on its next request <b>or circuit revalidation</b>" true for a screen
    /// that may sit on one circuit for a week — and it doubles as the <c>last_seen_at</c> heartbeat,
    /// since that touch is rate-limited to once a minute inside the authenticator.
    /// </summary>
    private async Task LoadAsync()
    {
        DisplayDeviceSession? session = await Devices.RevalidateAsync(_deviceIdentifier!.Value, _stopping);
        if (session is null)
        {
            _stage = DisplayStage.NotPaired;
            _qr = null;
            return;
        }

        _tableLabel = session.TableLabel;
        _deviceTableLabel = session.TableLabel;

        if (!session.TableIsActive)
        {
            // §4.1: deactivating a table stops its display rendering. The device stays paired.
            _stage = DisplayStage.TableOutOfService;
            _qr = null;
            return;
        }

        _stage = DisplayStage.Live;
        _qr = await JoinTokens.DescribeCurrentAsync(TableId, _stopping);

        TableSittingSummary? sitting = await Sittings.GetOpenSittingAsync(TableId, _stopping);
        _partySize = sitting?.MemberCount ?? 0;
        _refreshSequence++;
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// The window-aligned refresh (§4.3: "the display re-renders on a server timer aligned to the window
    /// boundary — fire at <c>(window_index+1) × rotation</c>"). The next boundary comes from the code
    /// just rendered, so the loop stays aligned without keeping its own notion of the window.
    /// </summary>
    private async Task RunRefreshLoopAsync()
    {
        while (!_stopping.IsCancellationRequested)
        {
            try
            {
                await Task.Delay(DelayUntilNextWindow(), _stopping);
                await InvokeAsync(RefreshAsync);
            }
            catch (OperationCanceledException)
            {
                return; // the circuit went away
            }
            catch (ObjectDisposedException)
            {
                return; // torn down mid-flight
            }
        }
    }

    private async Task RefreshAsync()
    {
        await LoadAsync();

        if (_stage == DisplayStage.NotPaired)
        {
            // Revoked while we were watching. A full-page navigation re-runs the middleware, which
            // clears the dead cookie, so the pairing screen greets it with "this display was
            // disconnected" rather than a bare form (§11.5).
            Navigation.NavigateTo(DisplayRoutes.Pair, forceLoad: true);
            return;
        }

        StateHasChanged();
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// Time until just after the next rotation boundary. The 250 ms of overshoot keeps the refresh on the
    /// far side of the boundary, so the code rendered is the new window's rather than the old one's; the
    /// floor and ceiling stop a clock jump from turning the loop into a spin or a long sleep.
    /// </summary>
    private TimeSpan DelayUntilNextWindow()
    {
        TimeSpan rotation = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(Options.TableJoinTokenRotationSeconds);
        DateTimeOffset now = Clock.UtcNow;
        DateTimeOffset boundary = _qr?.NextRotationAt ?? now + rotation;

        TimeSpan delay = boundary - now + TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(250);

        if (delay < TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(500))
        {
            return TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(500);
        }

        return delay > rotation ? rotation : delay;
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// §9 attaches the party-size chip to <c>SittingMemberJoined</c>, and a close empties the table, so
    /// both are re-read. The sitting identifier is deliberately not compared: the very notification that
    /// matters most — the first person joining — announces a sitting this surface has never seen, so
    /// filtering on a known id would drop it. One cheap scoped query per table event is the right trade.
    /// </summary>
    private void OnDomainNotification(DomainNotification notification)
    {
        if (notification is not SittingMemberJoined && notification is not SittingClosed)
        {
            return;
        }

        _ = InvokeAsync(async () =>
        {
            try
            {
                TableSittingSummary? sitting = await Sittings.GetOpenSittingAsync(TableId, _stopping);
                _partySize = sitting?.MemberCount ?? 0;
                StateHasChanged();
            }
            catch (OperationCanceledException)
            {
                // Disposed between the broadcast and the query; nothing to update.
            }
            catch (ObjectDisposedException)
            {
                // Same, one layer down.
            }
        });
    }

    public void Dispose()
    {
        if (_disposed)
        {
            return;
        }

        _disposed = true;
        _subscription?.Dispose();
        _lifetime.Cancel();
        _lifetime.Dispose();
    }
}

@* The landing page. It does two jobs: point a fresh deployment at /setup while no administrator
   exists (§3.6), and — since MainLayout deliberately carries at most one area link to keep the
   phone-sized header from wrapping onto three rows — be the one place every area a person can reach
   is listed. The links are role-gated with <AuthorizeView Roles="…">, matching the §3.7 policies:
   showing somebody a door that answers "access denied" is worse than not showing it. *@

@code {
    private bool _needsSetup;

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
    {
        // Point a fresh deployment at /setup while no administrator exists (§3.6). Best-effort: the
        // landing page must still render if the database is briefly unreachable (that is what
        // /healthz/ready is for), so a failure here simply hides the pointer.
        try
        {
            _needsSetup = !await Bootstrap.AdministratorExistsAsync();
        }
        catch (Exception exception) when (exception is not OperationCanceledException)
        {
            _needsSetup = false;
        }
    }
}

@page "/kitchen"
@attribute [Authorize(Policy = AuthorizationPolicies.Kitchen)]

@* The kitchen board (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §10, §11.2).

   Interactive server, prerendered, and the only surface in the tree that is expected to sit on one
   circuit for a whole service. Everything it shows is derived: the queue is the kitchen_pending_line
   view (§8.3), the Undo list is IKitchenBoardReads, the "86" panel is the menu. It holds no state of its
   own except the alert state, which is a browser-audio permission and therefore cannot be anything but
   circuit state (§10.3).

   Nothing here enforces §6.5. Every tap goes through IOrderWorkflow to the one transaction, which
   re-decides under the lock (§6.6) — so two cooks tapping the same line at the same moment produce one
   fulfillment and one refusal, and the refusal is shown rather than swallowed. What this surface
   refuses on its own it refuses only to make the answer immediate.

   The actor role is read from the principal rather than assumed: §6.2 lets kitchen OR administrator
   author a fulfillment, and an administrator covering the pass must not be recorded as the kitchen. *@

<PageTitle>Kitchen</PageTitle>

<section class="panel kitchen-board" id="kitchen-board-surface">
    <div class="kitchen-header">
        <div>
            <p class="eyebrow">@Options.RestaurantName</p>
            <h1>Kitchen</h1>
        </div>
        <div class="kitchen-header-status">
            @if (_alerts.HasUnseen)
            {
                @* §10.3: "a persistent, high-contrast visual badge with unseen-alert count". It is shown
                   whenever something is unacknowledged, armed or not — the badge is the record of what
                   arrived, and the sound is only how you find out sooner. *@
                <button type="button" class="kitchen-alert-badge" @onclick="AcknowledgeAlerts">
                    @_alerts.UnseenCount new @(_alerts.UnseenCount == 1 ? "alert" : "alerts")@(_alerts.UnseenReminderCount > 0 ? $" ({_alerts.UnseenReminderCount} overdue)" : string.Empty)
                    <span class="kitchen-alert-dismiss">tap to clear</span>
                </button>
            }

            @if (!_alerts.IsArmed)
            {
                <button type="button" class="button-primary kitchen-arm" @onclick="ArmSoundAsync">
                    Enable sound
                </button>
            }
            else if (_alerts.PlaybackFailed)
            {
                <button type="button" class="button-secondary kitchen-arm" @onclick="ArmSoundAsync">
                    Sound failed — try again
                </button>
            }
            else

            }

    </div>

    @if (_alerts.ShowsVisualFallback)

            @if (_alerts.PlaybackFailed)

                    Alerts are silent until you tap <strong>Enable sound</strong> — browsers block sound
                    until someone asks for it. Until then the badge above is the only warning.
                </text>
            }

    }

    @if (_actionNotice is { } actionNotice)
    {
        <p class="status-success" role="status">@actionNotice</p>
    }

    @if (_actionProblem is { } actionProblem)

    }

    @if (!_loaded)
    {
        <p class="lede">Loading the board…</p>
    }
    else
    {
        <p class="lede">
            @if (_queue.Count == 0)
            {
                <text>Nothing is waiting. New sends appear here the moment a guest presses Send.</text>
            }
            else
            {

                    @KitchenQueue.TotalLineCount(_queue) @(KitchenQueue.TotalLineCount(_queue) == 1 ? "line" : "lines")
                    outstanding across @_queue.Count @(_queue.Count == 1 ? "table" : "tables"), oldest first.
                </text>
            }
        </p>

        @* ---- the queue (§11.2) ----------------------------------------------------------------- *@
        @foreach (KitchenQueueTable table in _queue)
        {
            <article class="kitchen-table" @key="table.TableIdentifier">
                <header class="kitchen-table-header">
                    <h2>@table.TableLabel</h2>
                    <span class="kitchen-waiting">waiting @Waiting(table.OldestAddedAt)</span>
                </header>

                @foreach (KitchenQueueTicket ticket in table.Tickets)
                {
                    <section class="kitchen-ticket" @key="ticket.GuestOrderIdentifier">
                        <header class="kitchen-ticket-header">
                            <div>
                                <h3>@ticket.PersonName</h3>
                                <p class="kitchen-ticket-sends">
                                    sent @string.Join(", ", ticket.SendTimes.Select(instant => RestaurantClock.Time(instant)))
                                </p>
                            </div>
                            <button type="button" class="button-secondary kitchen-fulfill-all"
                                    disabled="@_busy"
                                    @onclick="() => FulfillTicketAsync(ticket)">
                                Fulfill all @ticket.LineCount
                            </button>
                        </header>

                        <ul class="kitchen-lines">
                            @foreach (KitchenQueueLine line in ticket.Lines)
                            {
                                <li class="kitchen-line @(line.HasNote ? "has-note" : string.Empty)"
                                    @key="line.OrderLineIdentifier">
                                    @* One tap on the line is one fulfillment event (§11.2). The whole row
                                       is the target because a cook is wearing gloves and looking at a
                                       pass, not aiming at a 24-pixel checkbox. *@
                                    <button type="button" class="kitchen-line-button"
                                            disabled="@_busy"
                                            @onclick="() => FulfillLineAsync(ticket, line)">
                                        <span class="kitchen-line-quantity">@line.Quantity×</span>
                                        <span class="kitchen-line-name">@line.MenuItemName</span>
                                        <span class="kitchen-line-action">Fulfill</span>
                                    </button>

                                    @if (line.CustomizationNote is { } note)
                                    {
                                        @* §11.2: "customization notes prominent". *@
                                        <p class="kitchen-line-note">@note</p>
                                    }
                                </li>
                            }
                        </ul>
                    </section>
                }
            </article>
        }

        @* ---- undo (§11.2) ------------------------------------------------------------------------ *@
        @if (_recentlyFulfilled.Count > 0)
        {
            <section class="kitchen-recent">
                <h2 class="kitchen-recent-heading">Just fulfilled</h2>
                <p class="muted">
                    Anything marked done in the last @((int)RecentFulfillmentWindow.TotalMinutes) minutes. Undo
                    puts it back on the board and tells the guest it is with the kitchen again.
                </p>

                <ul class="kitchen-recent-list">
                    @foreach (KitchenFulfilledLineView line in _recentlyFulfilled)
                    {
                        <li class="kitchen-recent-line" @key="line.OrderLineIdentifier">
                            <div class="kitchen-recent-main">
                                <span class="kitchen-recent-name">
                                    @line.Quantity× @line.MenuItemName
                                </span>
                                <span class="kitchen-recent-where">
                                    @line.TableLabel · @line.PersonName · @RestaurantClock.Time(line.FulfilledAt)
                                </span>
                            </div>
                            <button type="button" class="link-button"
                                    disabled="@_busy"
                                    @onclick="() => UndoFulfillmentAsync(line)">
                                Undo
                            </button>
                        </li>
                    }
                </ul>
            </section>
        }

        @* ---- the "86" panel (§7, §11.2) ---------------------------------------------------------- *@
        <section class="kitchen-eighty-six">
            <h2 class="kitchen-recent-heading">Availability (“86”)</h2>
            <p class="muted">
                Turning something off leaves it on the guest's menu marked <em>currently unavailable</em>
                and stops it being ordered. Orders already sent are untouched.
            </p>

            @if (_menu.Count == 0)
            {
                <p class="muted">There is nothing on the menu yet.</p>
            }
            else
            {
                <ul class="kitchen-menu">
                    @foreach (MenuItemSummary item in _menu)
                    {
                        <li class="kitchen-menu-item @(item.IsActive ? string.Empty : "is-off")"
                            @key="item.MenuItemIdentifier">
                            <span class="kitchen-menu-name">@item.Name</span>
                            <span class="kitchen-menu-state">
                                @(item.IsActive ? "On" : "86'd")
                            </span>
                            <button type="button"
                                    class="@(item.IsActive ? "button-secondary" : "button-primary")"
                                    disabled="@_busy"
                                    @onclick="() => ToggleMenuItemAsync(item)">
                                @(item.IsActive ? "Turn off" : "Bring back")
                            </button>
                        </li>
                    }
                </ul>
            }
        </section>
    }
</section>

@code {
    /// <summary>
    /// How far back the Undo list reaches (§11.2's "recently-fulfilled"). Long enough that a mis-tap
    /// noticed when the plate reaches the pass is still undoable, short enough that the panel does not
    /// become a second, stale copy of the service. Not configuration: §13 does not name it, and a
    /// setting nobody would ever change is a setting that only adds a way to be wrong.
    /// </summary>
    private static readonly TimeSpan RecentFulfillmentWindow = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(15);

    private readonly KitchenAlertState _alerts = new();

    // Captured once, so nothing ever touches _lifetime.Token after Dispose has run — the shape
    // TableDisplay and TableOrderSurface both use.
    private readonly CancellationTokenSource _lifetime = new();
    private CancellationToken _stopping;
    private IDisposable? _subscription;
    private bool _disposed;

    private Guid? _person;
    private OrderActorRole _actorRole = OrderActorRole.Kitchen;
    private bool _loaded;
    private bool _busy;

    private IReadOnlyList<KitchenQueueTable> _queue = [];
    private IReadOnlyList<KitchenFulfilledLineView> _recentlyFulfilled = [];
    private IReadOnlyList<MenuItemSummary> _menu = [];

    private string? _actionNotice;
    private string? _actionProblem;
    private int _announcedAlertToken;

    [CascadingParameter]
    private Task<AuthenticationState>? AuthenticationStateTask { get; set; }

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
    {
        _stopping = _lifetime.Token;

        if (AuthenticationStateTask is not null)
        {
            AuthenticationState state = await AuthenticationStateTask;
            _person = PersonPrincipal.IdentifierFor(state.User);

            // §6.2: a fulfillment may be authored by kitchen or administrator. Record what the person
            // actually is. Kitchen wins when they hold both, because that is the capacity they are
            // standing at this screen in.
            _actorRole = state.User.IsInRole(RestaurantRoles.Kitchen)
                ? OrderActorRole.Kitchen
                : OrderActorRole.Administrator;
        }

        await LoadAsync();
        _loaded = true;
    }

    protected override async Task OnAfterRenderAsync(bool firstRender)
    {
        if (firstRender)
        {
            // Only on the circuit: OnAfterRender does not run during prerendering, so no subscription is
            // created for a render about to be thrown away.
            _subscription = Broadcaster.Subscribe(OnDomainNotification);
        }

        if (_alerts.AlertToken == _announcedAlertToken)
        {
            return;
        }

        // Claim the token before awaiting, so the re-render this may cause cannot announce it twice.
        _announcedAlertToken = _alerts.AlertToken;

        if (!_alerts.IsArmed)
        {
            return;
        }

        bool played;
        try
        {
            played = await JavaScript.InvokeAsync<bool>(
                "myRestaurantKitchen.alert", _stopping, _alerts.LastAlertWasReminder);
        }
        catch (JSDisconnectedException)
        {
            return; // the circuit went away mid-alert
        }
        catch (OperationCanceledException)
        {
            return;
        }
        catch (JSException)
        {
            played = false;
        }

        // §10.3: "whenever playback fails" the visual badge is the fallback, so a failure has to be
        // recorded rather than shrugged off.
        bool changed = played ? _alerts.ReportPlaybackSucceeded() : _alerts.ReportPlaybackFailed();
        if (changed)
        {
            StateHasChanged();
        }
    }

    /// <summary>Everything the board shows, re-read in one pass. Three small, indexed queries.</summary>
    private async Task LoadAsync()
    {
        IReadOnlyList<KitchenPendingLineView> pending = await OrderReads
            .ListKitchenPendingLinesAsync(_stopping);

        _queue = KitchenQueue.Build(pending);

        _recentlyFulfilled = await KitchenReads
            .ListRecentlyFulfilledLinesAsync(Clock.UtcNow - RecentFulfillmentWindow, _stopping);

        _menu = await MenuDirectory.ListAsync(_stopping);
    }

    /// <summary>§11.2: "Tap a line → one <c>fulfillment</c> event".</summary>
    private Task FulfillLineAsync(KitchenQueueTicket ticket, KitchenQueueLine line)
        => AppendAsync(
            ticket.GuestOrderIdentifier,
            OrderEventType.Fulfillment,
            [new LineFulfilledOperation(line.OrderLineIdentifier)],
            $"{line.Quantity} × {line.MenuItemName} is away.");

    /// <summary>§11.2: "'fulfill all for this order' → one event, N operations".</summary>
    private Task FulfillTicketAsync(KitchenQueueTicket ticket)
        => AppendAsync(
            ticket.GuestOrderIdentifier,
            OrderEventType.Fulfillment,
            ticket.Lines.Select(line => (OrderOperation)new LineFulfilledOperation(line.OrderLineIdentifier)).ToArray(),
            $"{ticket.PersonName}'s order is away — {ticket.LineCount} {(ticket.LineCount == 1 ? "line" : "lines")}.");

    /// <summary>§11.2: "an Undo affordance on recently-fulfilled lines → <c>fulfillment_reversal</c>".</summary>
    private Task UndoFulfillmentAsync(KitchenFulfilledLineView line)
        => AppendAsync(
            line.GuestOrderIdentifier,
            OrderEventType.FulfillmentReversal,
            [new LineFulfillmentRevertedOperation(line.OrderLineIdentifier)],
            $"{line.Quantity} × {line.MenuItemName} is back on the board.");

    /// <summary>
    /// The one path every kitchen action takes. Through <see cref="IOrderWorkflow"/> so the commit is
    /// counted (§12) and broadcast (§9) — a fulfillment the guest's phone never hears about is exactly
    /// the badge that never turns green.
    /// </summary>
    private async Task AppendAsync(
        Guid guestOrderIdentifier,
        OrderEventType eventType,
        IReadOnlyList<OrderOperation> operations,
        string successMessage)
    {
        if (_person is not { } person || _busy || operations.Count == 0)
        {
            return;
        }

        _busy = true;
        _actionNotice = null;
        _actionProblem = null;

        try
        {
            AppendOrderEventResult result = await Workflow.AppendStaffEventAsync(
                guestOrderIdentifier,
                new ProposedOrderEvent(eventType, person, _actorRole, operations),
                _stopping);

            if (result.IsAppended)
            {
                _actionNotice = successMessage;

                // Acting on the board is acknowledging it: the cook has plainly seen what arrived.
                _alerts.Acknowledge();
            }
            else
            {
                _actionProblem = DescribeRefusal(result);
            }

            await LoadAsync();
        }
        catch (OperationCanceledException)
        {
            // The circuit went away mid-write. The transaction either committed or did not; either way
            // there is nobody left to tell.
        }
        finally
        {
            _busy = false;
        }
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// A refusal in plain words. The overwhelmingly likely cause is a race — two cooks on the same line,
    /// or a guest removing something a second before it was tapped — so the message says what to do
    /// (nothing; the board has already refreshed) rather than reading like a fault.
    /// </summary>
    private static string DescribeRefusal(AppendOrderEventResult result)
    {
        if (result.Outcome is AppendOrderEventOutcome.OrderNotFound or AppendOrderEventOutcome.SittingNotFound)
        {
            return "That table has been settled, so nothing more can be recorded against it.";
        }

        string reason = result.Errors.Count > 0
            ? result.Errors[0].Reason
            : "It was refused.";

        return $"Nothing was changed — {reason} The board has been refreshed.";
    }

    /// <summary>§11.2: "An '86' panel lists menu items with active toggles."</summary>
    private async Task ToggleMenuItemAsync(MenuItemSummary item)
    {
        if (_person is not { } person || _busy)
        {
            return;
        }

        _busy = true;
        _actionNotice = null;
        _actionProblem = null;

        try
        {
            SetMenuItemAvailabilityResult result = await MenuWorkflow
                .SetMenuItemActiveAsync(item.MenuItemIdentifier, !item.IsActive, person, _stopping);

            _actionNotice = result.Outcome switch
            {
                SetMenuItemAvailabilityOutcome.Changed when result.IsActive => $"{result.Name} is back on.",
                SetMenuItemAvailabilityOutcome.Changed => $"{result.Name} is 86'd.",
                SetMenuItemAvailabilityOutcome.AlreadyInThatState => $"{result.Name} was already set that way.",
                _ => null,
            };

            if (!result.ItemExists)
            {
                _actionProblem = "That item is no longer on the menu.";
            }

            await LoadAsync();
        }
        catch (OperationCanceledException)
        {
            // Circuit gone; nothing to update.
        }
        finally
        {
            _busy = false;
        }
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// §10.3's one-tap arm. The browser will only unlock audio inside a user gesture, so this has to be
    /// a click handler and cannot be done for the cook at page load.
    /// </summary>
    private async Task ArmSoundAsync()
    {
        bool armed;
        try
        {
            armed = await JavaScript.InvokeAsync<bool>("myRestaurantKitchen.arm", _stopping);
        }
        catch (JSDisconnectedException)
        {
            return;
        }
        catch (OperationCanceledException)
        {
            return;
        }
        catch (JSException)
        {
            armed = false;
        }

        _alerts.Arm(armed);

        // Do not retro-play everything that arrived before the cook found the button.
        _announcedAlertToken = _alerts.AlertToken;
    }

    private void AcknowledgeAlerts()
    {
        _alerts.Acknowledge();
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// §9 lists which notifications the kitchen re-queries on. All five that can change this screen are
    /// handled with one re-read: the queries are small and a kitchen is not a hot path.
    ///
    /// <para>Nothing is filtered by identifier here, unlike the table surface — the board is the whole
    /// restaurant by definition, so every one of these events is this board's business.</para>
    /// </summary>
    private void OnDomainNotification(DomainNotification notification)
    {
        bool concernsTheBoard = notification
            is OrderLinesChanged
            or LineFulfillmentChanged
            or SittingClosed
            or MenuChanged
            or KitchenAlert;

        if (!concernsTheBoard)
        {
            return;
        }

        KitchenAlertKind? alertKind = notification is KitchenAlert alert ? alert.Kind : null;

        _ = InvokeAsync(async () =>
        {
            if (_disposed)
            {
                return;
            }

            // Recorded here rather than on the broadcaster's thread: KitchenAlertState is a plain
            // counter, and the broadcaster fans out from whichever thread committed the event, so two
            // sends landing together could lose an increment. The renderer's dispatcher serializes every
            // mutation of it. It is recorded BEFORE the re-read so an alert still counts if the queries
            // below fail — a board that missed a query is recoverable, a board that missed an alert is
            // silent.
            if (alertKind is { } kind)
            {
                _alerts.Record(kind);
            }

            try
            {
                await LoadAsync();
                StateHasChanged();
            }
            catch (OperationCanceledException)
            {
                // Disposed between the broadcast and the query; nothing to update.
            }
            catch (ObjectDisposedException)
            {
                // Same, one layer down.
            }
        });
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// How long a ticket has been waiting, rendered coarsely. Coarse on purpose: a ticking
    /// seconds counter on twenty rows is a re-render per second per row and tells a cook nothing that
    /// "12m" does not. This is a duration, not an instant, so it does not go through
    /// <see cref="RestaurantTime"/> — there is no zone to render it in.
    /// </summary>
    private string Waiting(DateTimeOffset since)
    {
        TimeSpan elapsed = Clock.UtcNow - since;

        if (elapsed < TimeSpan.Zero)
        {
            elapsed = TimeSpan.Zero;
        }

        if (elapsed < TimeSpan.FromMinutes(1))
        {
            return "under a minute";
        }

        int minutes = (int)elapsed.TotalMinutes;
        if (minutes < 60)
        {
            return $"{minutes}m";
        }

        int hours = minutes / 60;
        return $"{hours}h {minutes % 60:D2}m";
    }

    public void Dispose()
    {
        if (_disposed)
        {
            return;
        }

        _disposed = true;
        _subscription?.Dispose();
        _lifetime.Cancel();
        _lifetime.Dispose();
    }
}

@inject IPasswordHasher<Person> PasswordHasher
@inject SignInManager<Person> SignInManager

@* The first-administrator bootstrap wizard (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §3.6). Reachable only while ZERO
   administrators exist; the moment one does, this page returns 404. Anonymous by design — there is no
   one to sign in as yet (the chicken-and-egg the whole feature resolves). Static SSR, like every
   account surface, because it writes cookies on the response (the accumulating setup ticket, and the
   authentication cookie once the administrator is created).

   The wizard is a single page driven by a Data-Protection-protected cookie (SetupTicket): collect
   account details → register a passkey → enroll TOTP → review and commit. The passkey and TOTP steps
   run their real ceremonies and cannot be skipped; nothing touches the database until the final step
   writes the whole account — person, passkey, TOTP secret, ten recovery codes, and the self-granted
   administrator role — in one advisory-locked transaction (FirstAdministratorBootstrap). *@

<PageTitle>Set up @Options.RestaurantName</PageTitle>

@if (_adminExists)
{
    <section class="panel account-panel">
        <p class="eyebrow">Setup</p>
        <h1>Setup is already complete</h1>
        <p class="lede">
            An administrator already exists for @Options.RestaurantName, so first-run setup is closed.
            If you are staff, sign in as usual.
        </p>
        <p><a href="@AccountRoutes.SignIn">Go to sign in</a></p>
    </section>
}
else if (_completed && _recoveryCodes is not null)
{
    <section class="panel account-panel">
        <p class="eyebrow">Setup complete</p>
        <h1>You are the administrator</h1>
        <p class="status-success" role="status">
            The administrator account <strong>@_completedUsername</strong> was created and you are now
            signed in.
        </p>

        <p class="totp-secret-label">Save these recovery codes now — this is the only time they are shown.</p>
        <p class="lede">
            Each works once, in place of your authenticator code, on the password sign-in. Keep them
            somewhere safe and offline.
        </p>
        <ul class="recovery-codes">
            @foreach (string recoveryCode in _recoveryCodes)
            {
                <li>@recoveryCode</li>
            }
        </ul>

        <div class="form-actions">
            <a class="button-primary" href="/administration">Go to administration</a>
            <a class="button-secondary" href="/">Home</a>
        </div>
    </section>
}
else
{
    <section class="panel account-panel">
        <p class="eyebrow">First-run setup</p>

        <ol class="setup-steps" aria-label="Setup progress">
            <li class="@StepClass(0)">Account</li>
            <li class="@StepClass(1)">Passkey</li>
            <li class="@StepClass(2)">Authenticator</li>
            <li class="@StepClass(3)">Finish</li>
        </ol>

        @if (_errorMessage is not null)
        {
            <p class="status-error" role="alert">@_errorMessage</p>
        }

        @if (_ticket is null)
        {
            @* Step 1 — account details. *@
            <h1>Create the first administrator</h1>
            <p class="lede">
                No administrator exists yet. Set one up now: choose a username and password, then add a
                passkey and an authenticator. All three are required — the passkey and the authenticator
                cannot be skipped.
            </p>

            <EditForm Model="AccountInput" method="post" OnValidSubmit="StartAsync" FormName="setup-account">
                <DataAnnotationsValidator />

                <div class="form-field">
                    <label for="username">Username</label>
                    <InputText id="username" @bind-Value="AccountInput.Username" autocomplete="username"
                               autocapitalize="none" spellcheck="false" autofocus />
                    <ValidationMessage For="@(() => AccountInput.Username)" />
                </div>

                <div class="form-field">
                    <label for="display-name">Display name <span class="optional">(optional)</span></label>
                    <InputText id="display-name" @bind-Value="AccountInput.DisplayName" autocomplete="name" />
                    <ValidationMessage For="@(() => AccountInput.DisplayName)" />
                </div>

@code {
    private SetupTicketProtector _protector = default!;
    private SetupTicket? _ticket;
    private bool _adminExists;
    private bool _completed;
    private string? _completedUsername;
    private IReadOnlyList<string>? _recoveryCodes;
    private string? _errorMessage;

    // Prepared once for the TOTP step so the same QR survives a mistyped-code re-render.
    private string _qrCodeSvg = string.Empty;
    private string _manualEntrySecret = string.Empty;

    [CascadingParameter]
    private HttpContext HttpContext { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm(FormName = "setup-account")]
    private AccountInputModel AccountInput { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm(FormName = "setup-passkey")]
    private PasskeyInputModel PasskeyInput { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromForm(FormName = "setup-totp")]
    private TotpInputModel TotpInput { get; set; } = default!;

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
    {
        // BL0008: a form POST binds these itself and may assign null, so defaults live here.
        AccountInput ??= new();
        PasskeyInput ??= new();
        TotpInput ??= new();
        _protector = new SetupTicketProtector(DataProtection);

        // The unlocked gate: if any administrator exists, /setup is gone (§3.6). The authoritative
        // re-check happens under the advisory lock at commit, so a race here is harmless.
        _adminExists = await Bootstrap.AdministratorExistsAsync(HttpContext.RequestAborted);
        if (_adminExists)
        {
            HttpContext.Response.StatusCode = StatusCodes.Status404NotFound;
            return;
        }

        if (HttpContext.Request.Cookies.TryGetValue(SetupCookie.Name, out string? cookie)
            && _protector.TryUnprotect(cookie, out SetupTicket? ticket)
            && ticket is not null
            && !ticket.HasExpired(Clock.UtcNow, SetupCookie.Lifetime))
        {
            _ticket = ticket;
            if (_ticket.Step == SetupStep.Totp && !string.IsNullOrEmpty(_ticket.TotpSecretBase32))
            {
                PrepareTotpDisplay(_ticket);
            }
        }
        else if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(cookie))
        {
            // Stale, tampered, or from another key: drop it and start clean.
            SetupCookie.Delete(HttpContext.Response);
            _errorMessage = "Your setup session expired. Please start again.";
        }
    }

    private async Task StartAsync()
    {
        if (_adminExists)
        {
            return;
        }

        string username = AccountInput.Username.Trim();
        string? displayName = string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(AccountInput.DisplayName)
            ? null
            : AccountInput.DisplayName.Trim();

        // Best-effort duplicate check; the person UNIQUE constraint and the commit are authoritative.
        if (await UserManager.FindByNameAsync(username) is not null)
        {
            _errorMessage = "That username is already taken. Please choose another.";
            return;
        }

        Guid personIdentifier = IdentifierFactory.Create();

        // Hash immediately so the plaintext is never carried in the ticket. The hasher ignores the
        // user argument (no per-user pepper, §3.2); a throwaway carrier is fine.
        string passwordHash = PasswordHasher.HashPassword(
            new Person { PersonIdentifier = personIdentifier, Username = username },
            AccountInput.Password);

        WriteTicketAndReload(new SetupTicket(
            personIdentifier,
            Clock.UtcNow,
            SetupStep.Passkey,
            username,
            displayName,
            passwordHash,
            Passkey: null,
            TotpSecretBase32: null));
    }

    private async Task RegisterPasskeyAsync()
    {
        if (_adminExists)
        {
            return;
        }

        if (_ticket is null || _ticket.Step != SetupStep.Passkey)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo(AccountRoutes.Setup);
            return;
        }

        if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(PasskeyInput.Error))
        {
            _errorMessage = "That passkey could not be added. Please try again.";
            return;
        }

        if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(PasskeyInput.CredentialJson))
        {
            _errorMessage = "Your browser did not provide a passkey.";
            return;
        }

        PasskeyAttestationResult attestation =
            await SignInManager.PerformPasskeyAttestationAsync(PasskeyInput.CredentialJson);
        if (!attestation.Succeeded || attestation.Passkey is null)
        {
            _errorMessage = "That passkey could not be registered. Please try again.";
            return;
        }

        UserPasskeyInfo info = attestation.Passkey;
        SetupPasskey passkey = new(
            info.CredentialId,
            info.PublicKey,
            (long)info.SignCount,
            info.Transports,
            Name: $"Passkey added {RestaurantClock.Date(Clock.UtcNow)}",
            info.IsUserVerified,
            info.IsBackupEligible,
            info.IsBackedUp);

        // Mint the authenticator secret now so the TOTP step's QR is stable across re-renders.
        string totpSecretBase32 = Base32Text.Encode(Rfc6238Totp.GenerateSecret());

        WriteTicketAndReload(_ticket with
        {
            Step = SetupStep.Totp,
            Passkey = passkey,
            TotpSecretBase32 = totpSecretBase32,
        });
    }

    private Task ConfirmTotpAsync()
    {
        if (_adminExists)
        {
            return Task.CompletedTask;
        }

        if (_ticket is null || _ticket.Step != SetupStep.Totp || string.IsNullOrEmpty(_ticket.TotpSecretBase32))
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo(AccountRoutes.Setup);
            return Task.CompletedTask;
        }

        if (!Base32Text.TryDecode(_ticket.TotpSecretBase32, out byte[] secret))
        {
            SetupCookie.Delete(HttpContext.Response);
            _ticket = null;
            _errorMessage = "Something went wrong with the setup code. Please start again.";
            return Task.CompletedTask;
        }

        string normalized = (TotpInput.Code ?? string.Empty).Replace(" ", string.Empty).Replace("-", string.Empty);
        if (!Rfc6238Totp.ValidateCode(secret, normalized, Clock.UtcNow))
        {
            // The QR was already prepared in OnInitializedAsync (step is still Totp); it re-renders.
            _errorMessage = "That code did not match. Check your authenticator and try again.";
            return Task.CompletedTask;
        }

        WriteTicketAndReload(_ticket with { Step = SetupStep.Review });
        return Task.CompletedTask;
    }

    private async Task FinishAsync()
    {
        if (_adminExists)
        {
            return;
        }

        if (_ticket is null
            || _ticket.Step != SetupStep.Review
            || _ticket.Passkey is null
            || string.IsNullOrEmpty(_ticket.TotpSecretBase32))
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo(AccountRoutes.Setup);
            return;
        }

        SetupPasskey stored = _ticket.Passkey;
        UserPasskeyInfo passkey = new(
            stored.CredentialId,
            stored.PublicKey,
            Clock.UtcNow, // placeholder; the bootstrap stamps created_at itself
            (uint)stored.SignatureCounter,
            stored.Transports,
            stored.IsUserVerified,
            stored.IsBackupEligible,
            stored.IsBackedUp,
            attestationObject: [],
            clientDataJson: [])
        {
            Name = stored.Name,
        };

        FirstAdministratorBootstrapResult result = await Bootstrap.CreateFirstAdministratorAsync(
            new NewAdministrator(
                _ticket.PersonIdentifier,
                _ticket.Username,
                _ticket.DisplayName,
                _ticket.PasswordHash,
                _ticket.TotpSecretBase32,
                passkey),
            HttpContext.RequestAborted);

        // Whatever happens next, the wizard is finished with the cookie.
        SetupCookie.Delete(HttpContext.Response);

        if (result.Status == FirstAdministratorBootstrapStatus.AdministratorAlreadyExists)
        {
            // Lost the race (or setup already ran): behave as if /setup is gone.
            _adminExists = true;
            _ticket = null;
            HttpContext.Response.StatusCode = StatusCodes.Status404NotFound;
            return;
        }

        // Created: sign the new administrator in on this response, then show the codes once.
        Person? administrator = await UserManager.FindByIdAsync(_ticket.PersonIdentifier.ToString());
        if (administrator is not null)
        {
            await SignInManager.SignInAsync(administrator, isPersistent: true);
        }

        _completedUsername = _ticket.Username;
        _recoveryCodes = result.RecoveryCodes;
        _completed = true;
        _ticket = null;
    }

    private void RestartAsync()
    {
        SetupCookie.Delete(HttpContext.Response);
        Navigation.NavigateTo(AccountRoutes.Setup);
    }

    // Writes the protected ticket cookie and follows post/redirect/get so a refresh does not re-post
    // the step. NavigateTo during static SSR surfaces as an HTTP redirect carrying the fresh cookie.
    private void WriteTicketAndReload(SetupTicket ticket)
    {
        SetupCookie.Write(HttpContext.Response, _protector.Protect(ticket));
        Navigation.NavigateTo(AccountRoutes.Setup);
    }

    private void PrepareTotpDisplay(SetupTicket ticket)
    {
        string provisioningUri = TotpProvisioningUri.Build(Options.RestaurantName, ticket.Username, ticket.TotpSecretBase32!);
        _qrCodeSvg = TotpQrCode.RenderSvg(provisioningUri);
        _manualEntrySecret = GroupForManualEntry(ticket.TotpSecretBase32!);
    }

    // The active step index (Account=0, Passkey=1, Authenticator=2, Finish=3).
    private int ActiveStepIndex => _ticket is null
        ? 0
        : _ticket.Step switch
        {
            SetupStep.Passkey => 1,
            SetupStep.Totp => 2,
            _ => 3,
        };

    private string StepClass(int index)
        => index == ActiveStepIndex ? "setup-step is-current"
            : index < ActiveStepIndex ? "setup-step is-done"
            : "setup-step";

    /// <summary>Groups the Base32 secret into space-separated blocks of four for easier manual entry.</summary>
    private static string GroupForManualEntry(string base32)
    {
        StringBuilder builder = new(base32.Length + (base32.Length / 4));
        for (int index = 0; index < base32.Length; index++)
        {
            if (index > 0 && index % 4 == 0)
            {
                builder.Append(' ');
            }

            builder.Append(base32[index]);
        }

        return builder.ToString();
    }

    private sealed class AccountInputModel
    {
        [Required(ErrorMessage = "Choose a username.")]
        [StringLength(64, MinimumLength = 3, ErrorMessage = "The username must be 3–64 characters.")]
        public string Username { get; set; } = string.Empty;

        [StringLength(120, ErrorMessage = "That display name is too long.")]
        public string? DisplayName { get; set; }

        [Required(ErrorMessage = "Choose a password.")]
        [StringLength(256, MinimumLength = 12, ErrorMessage = "Use at least 12 characters.")]
        public string Password { get; set; } = string.Empty;

        [Required(ErrorMessage = "Re-enter the password.")]
        [Compare(nameof(Password), ErrorMessage = "The passwords do not match.")]
        public string ConfirmPassword { get; set; } = string.Empty;
    }

    private sealed class TotpInputModel
    {
        [Required(ErrorMessage = "Enter the six-digit code from your authenticator app.")]
        public string Code { get; set; } = string.Empty;
    }
}

@code {
    private IReadOnlyList<TableSittingSummary> _sittings = [];
    private bool _loaded;

    [CascadingParameter]
    private Task<AuthenticationState>? AuthenticationStateTask { get; set; }

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
    {
        // The cascading authentication state is the circuit-safe way to read the principal: there is
        // no HttpContext once the component is interactive, and this works identically during the
        // static prerender pass (AddCascadingAuthenticationState is wired in AddRestaurantIdentity).
        if (AuthenticationStateTask is not null)
        {
            AuthenticationState state = await AuthenticationStateTask;
            if (PersonPrincipal.IdentifierFor(state.User) is { } person)
            {
                _sittings = await Sittings.ListOpenSittingsForPersonAsync(person);
            }
        }

        _loaded = true;
    }
}

@page "/table/{TableId:guid}"
@attribute [ExcludeFromInteractiveRouting]
@using MyRestaurant.DataAccess.Sittings
@using MyRestaurant.DataAccess.Tables
@using MyRestaurant.Domain.LiveUpdates
@using MyRestaurant.Domain.Security
@using MyRestaurant.Domain.Time
@using MyRestaurant.WebApplication.Tables
@inject ITableDirectory TableDirectory
@inject ITableJoinTokens JoinTokens

@inject ISittingMembership Membership
@inject JoinGrantProtector Grants
@inject IDomainEventBroadcaster Broadcaster

@* The table join flow and the member's table surface (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §4.4, §5.1, §11.1).

   Deliberately ANONYMOUS and static SSR. Anonymous because a guest scanning a table's QR for the
   first time has no account yet, and §4.4 requires the grant to be issued *before* the detour through
   sign-in — the whole point of the grant is that it survives that detour. Static SSR because the flow
   writes and clears a cookie and issues redirects, none of which a Blazor circuit can do.

   The four states this page resolves to, in the order §4.4 decides them:

     1. Member  — an authenticated member of this table's open sitting. Members bypass tokens
                  entirely: no query string is consulted, and a deactivated table does not evict
                  anyone (§4.1 stops *new* tokens and display rendering, not a sitting in progress).
     2. Confirm — a non-member holding a live grant, signed in. One button turns the grant into
                  membership.
     3. (redirect) — a non-member holding a live grant, anonymous: off to sign-in with this page as
                  the return URL. The grant cookie is already written, so the trip back needs no token.
     4. Expired — everything else, rendered as a friendly re-scan page at HTTP 200 with no detail
                  about *which* thing failed (§4.4: "no oracle detail"). An unknown table, a
                  deactivated table, a stale token, and a forged grant are indistinguishable here.

   The join itself is a post/redirect/get: the POST consumes the grant, opens or joins the sitting in
   one transaction (§5.1), broadcasts SittingMemberJoined only when a membership row was actually
   inserted (§9), and redirects back here so a refresh cannot re-post.

   The MEMBER stage hosts <TableOrderSurface> as an interactive-server island. Everything §11.1 asks
   for below the join — a basket, a Send that reports per-operation reasons, lines that re-badge when
   the kitchen fulfills them, a party total that moves when someone else orders, the flip to a settled
   bill on SittingClosed — is live, and none of it can happen on a statically rendered page. Splitting
   it this way keeps the cookie work where an HTTP response exists and the live work on a circuit,
   rather than compromising one for the other. The roster moved into the island for the same reason:
   §9 sends SittingMemberJoined to table members, and a statically rendered list cannot hear it. *@

<PageTitle>@PageTitleText</PageTitle>

@if (_stage == JoinStage.Member && _table is not null && _sitting is not null)
{
    <section class="panel table-panel">
        <p class="eyebrow">Your table</p>
        <h1>@_table.Label</h1>

        @if (_justJoined)
        {
            <p class="status-success" role="status">You have joined @(_table.Label).</p>
        }

        @if (!_table.IsActive)
        {
            <p class="status-error" role="alert">
                This table has been taken out of service. Your sitting is still open and your order is
                intact — nobody new can join by scanning, though. Please speak to the counter.
            </p>
        }

        <TableOrderSurface @rendermode="InteractiveServer"
                           TableId="@TableId"
                           SittingId="@_sitting.SittingIdentifier" />

        <p class="table-back"><a href="/table">All your tables</a></p>
    </section>
}
else if (_stage == JoinStage.Confirm && _table is not null)
{
    <section class="panel table-panel">
        <p class="eyebrow">Join a table</p>
        <h1>@_table.Label</h1>

        <p class="lede">
            You scanned the code for <strong>@_table.Label</strong>. Joining puts you on this table's
            party, so everyone here can see what has been ordered and the running total.
        </p>

        @if (_openSittingMemberCount > 0)
        {

                @_openSittingMemberCount @(_openSittingMemberCount == 1 ? "person is" : "people are")

        {

            <AntiforgeryToken />

                <a class="button-secondary" href="/">Not now</a>
            </div>

            minute@(Options.TableJoinGrantMinutes == 1 ? "" : "s") from the moment you scanned.
        </p>
    </section>
}
else

@code {
    /// <summary>Which of the §4.4 outcomes this request resolved to. A redirect never reaches a stage.</summary>
    private enum JoinStage
    {
        /// <summary>Friendly re-scan page (§4.4) — the catch-all, and the default before anything is decided.</summary>
        Expired,

        /// <summary>Signed in, holding a live grant, not yet a member: offer the join button.</summary>
        Confirm,

        /// <summary>A member of this table's open sitting: the table surface itself.</summary>
        Member,
    }

    private JoinStage _stage = JoinStage.Expired;
    private RestaurantTableSummary? _table;
    private TableSittingSummary? _sitting;
    private int _openSittingMemberCount;
    private bool _justJoined;

    [Parameter]
    public Guid TableId { get; set; }

    [CascadingParameter]
    private HttpContext HttpContext { get; set; } = default!;

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery(Name = "token")]
    private string? Token { get; set; }

    [SupplyParameterFromQuery(Name = "joined")]
    private string? Joined { get; set; }

    private TimeSpan GrantLifetime => TimeSpan.FromMinutes(Options.TableJoinGrantMinutes);

    private string TablePath => $"/table/{TableId}";

    private string PageTitleText => _stage switch
    {
        JoinStage.Member when _table is not null => _table.Label,
        JoinStage.Confirm when _table is not null => $"Join {_table.Label}",
        _ => "Join a table",
    };

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
    {
        CancellationToken cancellationToken = HttpContext.RequestAborted;
        bool isGet = HttpMethods.IsGet(HttpContext.Request.Method);

        _table = await TableDirectory.GetTableAsync(TableId, cancellationToken);
        if (_table is null)
        {
            // No oracle: an unknown table reads exactly like a stale code (§4.4).
            _stage = JoinStage.Expired;
            return;
        }

        Guid? personIdentifier = PersonPrincipal.IdentifierFor(HttpContext.User);

        // (1) Members bypass tokens entirely (§4.4) — and a deactivated table does not evict them.
        if (personIdentifier is { } member)
        {
            _sitting = await Sittings.GetOpenSittingForMemberAsync(TableId, member, cancellationToken);
            if (_sitting is not null)
            {
                // The roster, the order, and the totals are the island's job from here — this page
                // stops at "you are a member of this sitting, here is the identifier".
                _stage = JoinStage.Member;
                _justJoined = isGet && string.Equals(Joined, "yes", StringComparison.Ordinal);
                return;
            }
        }

        // (2) A non-member cannot join a table that is out of service (§4.1).
        if (!_table.IsActive)
        {
            _stage = JoinStage.Expired;
            return;
        }

        // (3) A presented token is always validated on a GET, so the §4.3 metric counts every scan —
        // even when a grant is already held. A valid one (re)issues the grant and restarts its clock.
        // The join POST re-posts to this same URL, query string and all; re-validating there would
        // double-count one scan, so the metric stays on the navigation that actually is a scan.
        bool holdsGrant = false;
        if (isGet && !string.IsNullOrEmpty(Token))
        {
            JoinTokenValidationResult validation = await JoinTokens.ValidateAsync(TableId, Token, cancellationToken);
            if (validation == JoinTokenValidationResult.Valid)
            {
                JoinGrantCookie.Write(
                    HttpContext.Response,
                    Grants.Protect(new JoinGrant(TableId, Clock.UtcNow)),
                    GrantLifetime);
                holdsGrant = true;
            }
        }

        // (4) No usable token is not the end: an unconsumed grant from an earlier scan still counts.
        // That is what carries the flow back from sign-in, where the return URL has no token (§4.4).
        holdsGrant = holdsGrant || TryReadUsableGrant();

        if (!holdsGrant)
        {
            _stage = JoinStage.Expired;
            return;
        }

        if (personIdentifier is null)
        {
            // Anonymous with a live grant → sign in (or register) and come straight back here (§4.4).
            Navigation.NavigateTo($"{AccountRoutes.SignIn}?ReturnUrl={Uri.EscapeDataString(TablePath)}");
            return;
        }

        // Purely for the confirmation copy — how full the table already is. Skipped on the join POST,
        // which either redirects or falls to the expired page and never renders that sentence.
        if (isGet)
        {
            TableSittingSummary? openSitting = await Sittings.GetOpenSittingAsync(TableId, cancellationToken);
            _openSittingMemberCount = openSitting?.MemberCount ?? 0;
        }

        _stage = JoinStage.Confirm;
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// Turns the held grant into membership (§4.4, §5.1). Every precondition is re-checked here rather
    /// than trusted from the render that drew the button: a POST is a separate request, and the grant
    /// may have expired, been spent, or never have matched this table at all.
    /// </summary>
    private async Task JoinAsync()
    {
        CancellationToken cancellationToken = HttpContext.RequestAborted;

        if (PersonPrincipal.IdentifierFor(HttpContext.User) is not { } person)
        {
            Navigation.NavigateTo($"{AccountRoutes.SignIn}?ReturnUrl={Uri.EscapeDataString(TablePath)}");
            return;
        }

        if (!TryReadUsableGrant())
        {
            JoinGrantCookie.Delete(HttpContext.Response);
            _stage = JoinStage.Expired;
            return;
        }

        JoinTableResult result = await Membership.JoinTableAsync(TableId, person, cancellationToken);

        // Single-use, whatever the outcome: a spent or refused grant must never be replayable (§4.4).
        JoinGrantCookie.Delete(HttpContext.Response);

        if (result.Outcome == JoinTableOutcome.TableUnavailable)
        {
            _stage = JoinStage.Expired;
            return;
        }

        // After commit, and only when a membership row was really inserted (§9: "fired on: membership
        // insert"). An idempotent re-join writes nothing and so announces nothing.
        if (result.MembershipInserted && result.SittingIdentifier is { } sittingIdentifier)
        {
            Broadcaster.Publish(new SittingMemberJoined(sittingIdentifier));
        }

        Navigation.NavigateTo($"{TablePath}?joined=yes");
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// True when the request carries a grant that is ours, intact, names <b>this</b> table, and has not
    /// aged past <c>TABLE_JOIN_GRANT_MINUTES</c>. The lifetime is judged against the protected
    /// <c>issued_at</c>, not the cookie's own expiry, because only the former is beyond the guest's reach.
    /// </summary>
    private bool TryReadUsableGrant()
        => Grants.TryUnprotect(JoinGrantCookie.Read(HttpContext.Request), out JoinGrant? grant)
            && grant is not null
            && grant.IsUsableFor(TableId, Clock.UtcNow, GrantLifetime);
}

@* The guest ordering surface (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §6, §7, §9, §11.1).

   An INTERACTIVE ISLAND inside a static-SSR page, which is the one structural decision in this file
   worth reading twice. /table/{id} is [ExcludeFromInteractiveRouting] because the join flow writes the
   grant cookie and issues redirects, and a Blazor circuit can do neither. But everything §11.1 asks for
   below the join — a basket that survives a mis-tap, a Send that reports per-operation reasons, lines
   that re-badge when the kitchen fulfills them, a party total that moves when someone else orders — is
   live. So the page stays static and hosts this component with @@rendermode="InteractiveServer". The
   parent keeps the cookie work; this keeps the circuit.

   It is deliberately given only the two identifiers it needs and re-derives everything else. The person
   comes from the cascading authentication state rather than from a parameter, so the component is
   correct on its own terms and not merely correct because its caller was careful; membership and
   openness are re-read on every pass, which is what makes the §11.1 flip to a settled view happen
   without anyone telling this component that the counter closed the sitting.

   Nothing here enforces §6.5. The transaction does, under the lock, against a menu it re-reads there
   (§6.6). What this surface refuses — an unavailable item, a quantity outside 1–100, a tick on a line
   that is no longer the guest's to remove — it refuses only so the answer arrives at the moment of the
   tap instead of after a round trip. *@
